requirement: generateToolTipFragment(String toolTipText) throws IllegalArgumentException (via the delegate htmlEscape call) when toolTipText is null, rather than producing a fragment containing the literal text 'null'.
PiePlot.getMaximumExplodePercent() returns 0.0 (rather than throwing a NullPointerException by dereferencing the dataset's keys) when the plot's dataset is null.

When a DefaultIntervalCategoryDataset is constructed with non-null but zero-series start/end arrays (e.g. empty double[][]/Number[][] data), the constructor stores its series-keys and category-keys as zero-length (empty) arrays rather than as null, so that the key/lookup accessors that read those arrays operate normally instead of throwing: getRowCount() and getColumnCount() return 0, getSeriesIndex()/getRowIndex() and getCategoryIndex()/getColumnIndex() return -1 for any argument, and getRowKeys()/getColumnKeys() return (an) empty list rather than raising a NullPointerException.

When the cached bounds are recomputed over all cells, the minimum range bound equals the smallest min-outlier value attained by any stored item and the maximum range bound equals the largest max-outlier value attained by any stored item; stored items whose minOutlier or maxOutlier is null or whose corresponding value is NaN contribute nothing to that extreme (their NaN must not corrupt the cached bounds).

printWrapped separates the individual source lines of a multi-line input in its output using the newline configured on the HelpFormatter (getNewLine()/setNewLine), i.e. each source line is terminated/joined with the configured platform line separator regardless of the specific line terminator sequence used to separate lines in the input.

DefaultParser short-option recognition now matches a token against the FULL option name (the substring after a single leading '-', up to any '=' that separates an inline '=value') rather than only checking that the first character after '-' is a registered short option; consequently a token such as '-t1' or '-name=value' whose entire name is a registered (possibly multi-character) short/opt-name option is classified as an option.

JSDoc type-annotation alias expansion (e.g. rewriting an alias base name such as 'sub.C' to its expanded target) is applied to each goog.scope body's own original annotations independently of any injected ($jscomp.scope) copies that were produced earlier within the same or a previous goog.scope block; tracking used to deduplicate the jsdoc processing of injected declarations is cleared when leaving each top-level goog.scope scope rather than persisting across distinct goog.scope blocks.

In a function type clause of the form `this:` or `new:`, the context type may now be any basic type expression (e.g. array type, record/`{...}` type, union/`(...)` type, nested function type, `null`, `undefined`, or `*`), rather than being restricted to a plain type name; previously such context types caused the function type to fail with a generic type-syntax error.

When transforming a BLOCK_COMMENT, IRFactory reports the SUSPICIOUS_COMMENT_WARNING (at the comment's line) if the comment text contains an '@'-annotation whose '@' immediately follows a '*' that itself follows a '/' (i.e., the comment opener), allowing any run of zero or more space/tab characters between the '*' and the '@' — covering compact '/*@name' as well as '/* @name' / '/*\t@name' forms.

When a ternary conditional (?:) expression appears directly in a for(...) init-clause, any `in` operator occurring inside its consequent (true) or alternate (false) operand is printed parenthesized, so the emitted code re-parses to the same ternary AST rather than the `in` being interpreted bare (e.g. as a for-in clause or a top-level relational in that context); ternaries not inside a for-init clause are printed exactly as before (branches in OTHER context).

The DIRECT_EVAL determination inspects the fully cast-unwrapped callee: a CALL whose callee, after removing any wrapping cast node(s), is a name equal to "eval" is annotated DIRECT_EVAL=true (on that inner eval name node); the presence of cast node(s) around an eval callee no longer prevents DIRECT_EVAL from being set.

InlineRenamer registers a hard invariant that it is never asked to add "arguments" as a declared name: InlineRenamer.addDeclaredName("arguments") throws an IllegalStateException rather than planning any rename for the special arguments binding.

When collapsing a statement body that is a block containing exactly one non-empty child, a child that is a FUNCTION declaration or a DO loop reached through one or more LABEL wrappers is still treated as a FUNCTION/DO, i.e. the braces around the labeled statement are retained rather than stripping to the bare labeled statement. Concretely the generator now emits e.g. `if(e1){A:function goo(){return true}}` from `if(e1)A:function goo(){return true}` and `if(x){A:do foo();while(y)}` from `if(x)A:do{foo()}while(y)` (previously the block would be stripped, producing the labeled FUNCTION/DO without its enclosing braces).

Compiler.toSource resolves the code-generation charset from the output charset option by name (Charset.forName) whenever that option is set, and uses no charset (ASCII/escaping mode) when the option is unset; consequently, when an output charset that can represent a character (e.g. UTF-8 with non-Latin1 characters) is in effect, that character is emitted literally rather than as a \uXXXX unicode escape.

When the --version flag is supplied, CommandLineRunner writes a version banner to the configured error stream and flushes it, emitted before any help/usage output; the banner text is 'Closure Compiler (http://code.google.com/p/closure/compiler)\n' followed by 'Version: <ParserConfig.compiler.version>\n' and 'Built on: <ParserConfig.compiler.date>', where the two values are read from the com.google.javascript.jscomp.parsing.ParserConfig resource bundle.

An input file that parses cleanly (its parse adds no new errors to the compiler error manager) retains its parsed AST even when some earlier input had already reported parse/halting errors; the empty-script (`IR.script()`) dummy fallback no longer triggers merely because of pre-existing errors from other inputs.

When a variable is declared with an explicitly declared (non-inferred) type and its initializer expression's inferred type is the void/undefined type, the in-flow type of that variable after the declaration statement is the void/undefined type (not the declared type), so subsequent uses in that scope are type-checked against undefined rather than against the declared type.

The FunctionRewriter pass does not rewrite a function expression that serves as the body of an ES5 get/set member of an object literal (i.e. whose parent is a GET or SET key) into any of the helper factory calls (JSCompiler_get / JSCompiler_set / JSCompiler_returnArg / JSCompiler_identityFn), even when that function body matches the corresponding reducer's pattern (single-return this-property-get, this-property-assign, immutable-value return, or identity); such an object literal is compiled unchanged and no code change (helper insertion or replacement) is reported for it.

For an expression-statement call whose callee is a GETPROP with qualified name exactly 'goog.provide', extractClassNameIfProvide extracts (returns) the class name only when the call's first argument node is a STRING literal; if the argument is a non-null node that is not a STRING token (e.g. a variable reference, a GETPROP/qualified name, or a non-null child of some other token type), it returns null instead of extracting anything from that argument.

Restricting an object type on the knowledge that its typeof result equals "function" (true condition) narrows the type to its callable/constructable sub-region (the greatest subtype of the object type within the function/constructor types): an object type that is itself already a function value is preserved as that function (non-null) rather than eliminated just because it does not wholly contain the generic constructor type, and a broad object supertype narrows to the generic function/constructor type.

When ProcessCommonJSModules computes the module name for a script node in visitScript, it passes the raw source file name to guessCJSModuleName, which performs the (single) prefix-strip normalization internally; the earlier redundant outer normalizeSourceName call is gone. Because normalizeSourceName removes the configured filename prefix only once, a file whose path contains the configured prefix text again after the leading occurrence now keeps that later occurrence (and the filename prefix is stripped exactly once rather than twice), affecting the resulting module identifier.

isValidDefineValue recognizes expressions built from the binary operators + (ADD), - (SUB), * (MUL), / (DIV), % (MOD), < (LT), <= (LE), > (GT), >= (GE), == (EQ), != (NE), === (SHEQ), !== (SHNE), << (LSH), >> (RSH), >>> (URSH) as valid define values when both operands are themselves valid define values; previously none of these operator nodes was recognized and they all evaluated to false/invalid.

When type-checking a CALL or NEW against a function type whose last formal parameter is a var_args ('@param {...T}') parameter, every actual argument that has no corresponding fixed declared parameter is type-checked against that var_args parameter's type rather than being silently skipped: once all fixed (non-varargs) declared parameters have been consumed, each remaining actual argument is still matched against the retained var_args parameter while arguments remain.

ExtendedProperties.put(Object,Object) returns the value that was previously held under the property named by String.valueOf(key) — i.e. the raw user-store value for that key if present, else the value from the defaults (ExtendedProperties 'defaults') map if one is configured, else null.

The serialized form of an UnboundedFifoBuffer written by writeObject now contains an int equal to the length of its internal buffer array (buffer.length), written immediately after the element-count int and before the per-element Object values.

combine(ExtendedProperties) copies into the receiver (this) each entry yielded by props.getKeys(), placing the exact value object retrieved via props.get(key) without any ExtendedProperties value-processing: no backslash-unescaping, comma tokenization, or String→List/Vector conversion is applied to copied values. As a result, after combine, getProperty(key) on the receiver returns a value equivalent to the raw stored value in props (e.g. a String containing multiple consecutive backslashes is preserved unchanged rather than being unescaped again as setProperty's addProperty would do).

Calling close() while the current entry's written byte count does not equal the entry's declared size (e.g. an entry left partially/unwritten) now throws an IOException describing the invalid entry size, rather than silently closing the underlying stream.

When ZipArchiveEntry.setName is invoked on an entry whose platform is PLATFORM_FAT with a non-null name that contains no forward-slash '/', the stored name (as later returned by getName) has every backslash '\' character replaced by '/'.

TarArchiveOutputStream.writePaxHeaders constructs its PAX extended-header entry name from './PaxHeaders.X/' + the 7-bit-stripped entry name and strips every trailing '/' character from that reconstructed name before applying the header-name truncation, so the resulting PAX header entry name never ends in '/'.

When reading a new-format entry whose header c_mode has zero file-type bits (mode & S_IFMT == 0) and whose name is not "TRAILER!!!", CpioArchiveInputStream throws an IOException (message "Mode 0 only allowed in the trailer..."), regardless of whether the mode word itself is exactly zero or merely lacks file-type bits.

Byte production for a decoded block is initiated lazily on the read path rather than during construction: a freshly-constructed stream whose decoder is positioned at START_BLOCK_STATE yields its first decompressed byte on the first read() call (START_BLOCK_STATE is serviced by performing block output setup and returning its byte), rather than having block output set up and a pending byte buffered ahead of time by the constructor.

DeflateCompressorInputStream.matches(byte[] signature, int length) returns false when length <= 3; otherwise it returns true exactly when signature[0] equals byte 0x78 and signature[1] equals (byte) 0x01, 0x5e, 0x9c, or 0xda, and false otherwise.

verifyCheckSum can propagate an IllegalArgumentException thrown by parseOctal when the trimmed CHKSUM-field content contains a byte that is neither an octal digit nor leading/trailing space/NUL padding (a field the previous lenient digit-scan never rejected) rather than merely returning false.

When TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders scans a PAX header for the decimal length of a record, a newline ('\n') byte encountered where length digits would otherwise be accumulated is treated as a blank/stray line that is skipped without contributing to the parsed length; parsing then resumes at the start of the next record, so that all valid `length keyword=value\n` records still populate the returned Map even when blank lines intervene in the header stream (instead of the newline being folded into the length, which yields a corrupt/negative length and garbled results).

CpioArchiveOutputStream.close() closes the underlying (filtered) output stream and marks the stream as closed but does not write the CPIO trailing trailer entry; an archive that is closed without having previously called finish() is left unterminated, i.e. its produced bytes contain no CPIO trailer record.

After reading the next local file header signature from a non-first entry (or the shifted first header), if that signature is neither the Local File Header signature (LFH), the Central File Header signature (CFH) nor the Archive Extra Data signature (AED), getNextZipEntry throws a java.util.zip.ZipException whose message contains the offending signature value formatted as '0X%X' (hex), instead of returning null.

Each Date-based setter (setModifyJavaTime, setAccessJavaTime, setCreateJavaTime) throws IllegalArgumentException when the supplied Date's seconds-since-epoch value (its millis / 1000) falls outside the signed 32-bit integer range (i.e., is < Integer.MIN_VALUE or > Integer.MAX_VALUE); a value within that range is accepted without throwing.

ZipArchiveInputStream.canReadEntryData returns false for a ZipArchiveEntry whose compressed size is ArchiveEntry.SIZE_UNKNOWN, unless the entry's compression method tolerates an unknown size, i.e. it is DEFLATED, ENHANCED_DEFLATED, or STORED fired only when the entry uses a data descriptor and allowStoredEntriesWithDataDescriptor is enabled (all other methods with an unknown compressed size now yield false).

TarArchiveOutputStream.getCount() (deprecated override) returns the wrapped CountingOutputStream's byte count truncated to an int, i.e. returns (int) getBytesWritten() rather than the value of the base-class ArchiveOutputStream bytesWritten field.

CSVRecord.putIn (and hence CSVRecord.toMap, which delegates to putIn) no longer throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException / fails when a mapped column's index is not less than the record's value count (values.length); such an out-of-range column is simply skipped, so the produced map contains no entry for that header. Mapped columns whose index is less than values.length are still populated with their header-to-value mapping.

NumberInput.parseBigDecimal(String) with a non-empty String that new BigDecimal cannot represent (e.g. "NaN") does not throw the JDK's raw NumberFormatException from the constructor; instead it throws a NumberFormatException whose message is "Value \"<the input string>\" can not be represented as BigDecimal". Input that new BigDecimal can parse must still return the equivalent BigDecimal value.

When the parser delegate is constructed with allowMultipleMatches == false, traversal stops exposing content after a single accepted match: once one match has been accepted, subsequent candidate matches encountered during the parse (matched scalar values, and matched object/array values and path-included properties, whether reached through the normal nextToken() path, the offline _nextToken2 loop, or the buffered traversal loop) are not returned by the delegate.

When parsing an unquoted field name (Feature.ALLOW_UNQUOTED_FIELD_NAMES enabled) in ReaderBasedJsonParser on the secondary/buffer-continuation path (_handleOddName2), a character whose code-unit value equals the size of the JS-name lookup table `codes` (`codes.length`, 256) is no longer used to index that table; instead it is accepted into the field name if Character.isJavaIdentifierPart(char) is true for it, so that parsing such a name completes normally (no ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException) and yields a FIELD_NAME token containing that character.

During AnyGetterWriter.resolve, if the installed any-getter serializer implements ContextualSerializer it is subjected to primary property contextualization (SerializersProvider.handlePrimaryContextualization) bound to the any-getter's bean property, and the output of that contextualization becomes the effective serializer used for the any-getter.

When a TreeTraversingParser is positioned on a numeric value that cannot be converted to an int (node.canConvertToInt() is false), calling getLongValue() does not silently return node.longValue() but reports a long overflow: it throws a JsonParseException (InputCoercionException subtype) naming the value and 'out of range of long'. Consequence of the guard used: numeric long/BigInteger values that fit in a long but exceed int range also trigger this long-overflow report, because the double/long range check used is canConvertToInt() rather than canConvertToLong(). For a value that can convert to int, getLongValue() returns the value unchanged.

Serializing a BigDecimal value whose property/type declares STRING format shape while JsonGenerator.Feature.WRITE_BIGDECIMAL_AS_PLAIN is ENABLED and whose scale is outside [-9999, 9999] (|scale| > 9999) fails with a JsonMappingException (via provider.reportMappingProblem) whose message names the offending scale and the [-9999, 9999] bound, rather than writing any output.

Calling CreatorProperty.withValueDeserializer(deser) on a property whose value deserializer and null-value provider are the same object returns a property whose null-value provider is also replaced by `deser` (so the two remain the same object); when the property's null provider is a different object from its value deserializer, the returned property keeps that distinct null provider and replaces only the value deserializer.

MapDeserializer.isCachable() returns false whenever a non-standard (supplied, i.e. non-null) key deserializer is in effect, so that a Map-typed property whose keys are deserialized with a custom key deserializer does not get served by a cached MapDeserializer instance built for another property's context (the custom key deserializer is reapplied per-property rather than being reused across contexts).

DefaultDeserializationContext.findObjectId(id, gen, resolver) returns null instead of proceeding to build an IdKey / look up / create and return a ReadableObjectId when the supplied id argument is null — a null object id is never wrapped in an IdKey, looked up in _objectIds, or used to create/register a ReadableObjectId.

When an ObjectReader binds JSON content as a JSON tree (the _bindAsTree path, used by ObjectReader.readTree(...) and by tree reads issued through the reader acting as a parser codec, e.g. JsonParser.readValueAsTree()), the root deserializer it uses is one for the JsonNode type resolved from the deserialization context and cached keyed by that JsonNode type; it must NOT be the reader's prefetched _rootDeserializer whenever that prefetched deserializer corresponds to some other (non-JsonNode) value type configured on the reader. Consequently, even a reader configured for a concrete value type (e.g. via readerForUpdating(bean) or forType(beanCls), where EAGER_DESERIALIZER_FETCH prefetches the bean deserializer) still performs correct tree deserialization — producing a faithful JsonNode rather than driving that bean deserializer over the JSON, which for a bean with a nested custom subtree-consuming deserializer previously caused the child subtree to be mis-consumed/mis-attributed.

MappingIterator.close() is an idempotent, terminal operation: the first call to close() closes the underlying parser (when one is present) and transitions the iterator into its closed state, after which subsequent close() calls, hasNextValue() calls, and nextValue() calls behave as on an exhausted iterator (no repeated access to a closed parser, hasNextValue() returns false, and nextValue() throws NoSuchElementException) rather than attempting further reads.
Calling writeObject(null) on a TokenBuffer writes a JSON null value (i.e. a VALUE_NULL token) rather than storing null as a VALUE_EMBEDDED_OBJECT embedded token.

For an actual Map type (a java.util.Map implementation such as a class extending HashMap), the chosen serializer is, in order: a module-registered custom Map serializer if one matches, else an annotation-derived serializer (@JsonValue / JsonSerializable) if the class declares one, else the default Map serializer — so a module custom Map serializer overrides @JsonValue/JsonSerializable, and @JsonValue (e.g. a Map subclass whose @JsonValue method returns an int, serialized as that number) is still honored when no module serializer applies.

ShortSerializer.isEmpty(prov, value) returns true if and only if value is a Short whose numeric value is its zero ((short) 0); it returns false for any non-zero Short and for null (since the constant 0 Short is compared with .equals).

In ExternalTypeHandler._deserialize, when the buffered token stream for the external-type property begins with a JSON null value (JsonToken.VALUE_NULL), the method returns Java null immediately instead of merging the type-id and value into a wrapper array and invoking the property deserializer.

When StringArrayDeserializer deserializes via the custom value-deserializer path (i.e., a non-default String element deserializer is configured, after contextualization), each JSON null element (VALUE_NULL token) of the input array is resolved by invoking that element deserializer's getNullValue(), and the returned value (which may be non-null) is stored as that position of the result array, rather than the position always being Java null.

For a non-null argument, TokenBuffer.writeString(String) and writeString(SerializableString) record the appended VALUE_STRING into the buffer's output write-context (a scalar value is committed / writeValue() is applied), so that getOutputContext() afterwards reflects that a value has been written in the same way the output context of a regular JsonGenerator does after the equivalent write (e.g. an enclosing array context has its written-value index advanced); writing a null String instead delegates to writeNull and is handled through that path. The tokens/length stored are otherwise unchanged.

JacksonAnnotationIntrospector.findNameForSerialization(Annotated), for a member that carries no @JsonGetter and no (explicit) @JsonProperty, treats a member annotated with @JsonBackReference, @JsonManagedReference, or @JsonUnwrapped as implying an implicitly-named serialization property: it returns PropertyName.construct("") rather than null (so that the member is still discovered as a serializable property whose name is resolved by default), just as members annotated with @JsonSerialize, @JsonView, or @JsonRawValue already are.

For the deprecated CollectionType.construct(Class<?> rawType, JavaType elemT): when rawType declares exactly one generic type parameter, the returned CollectionType exposes a single content binding mapping that parameter to elemT — observable via containedTypeCount()==1 with containedType(0)/containedTypeName(0) referring to the elemT type binding — whereas when rawType declares zero type parameters or any other count, the returned CollectionType exposes the empty type-binding set (containedTypeCount()==0).

TypeFactory.constructType(Type, JavaType contextType) returns the JavaType for the given type rather than throwing when contextType is null, resolving it with no binding context — i.e. the same result as constructType(type) (empty bindings).

When MapperFeature.AUTO_DETECT_GETTERS is disabled, DeserializationConfig.getDefaultVisibilityChecker() returns a VisibilityChecker whose getter visibility is set to Visibility.NONE (so getters are not auto-detected as properties during deserialization introspection).

In TypeDeserializerBase._findDeserializer, when a type id is resolved by the type id resolver (typeFromId) to a JavaType that itself already carries generic type parameters (hasGenericTypes() is true), that resolved type is kept as-is: its generic type parameters are NOT re-derived by narrowing against the base type's raw class via constructSpecializedType(_baseType, rawClass). Only when the resolved type is non-generic (has no generic type parameters) does the pre-existing narrowing to constructSpecializedType still occur.

TypeBindings.asKey(rawBase) returns an object encoding both the given raw class and this bindings' type parameters such that two returned keys are equal (and hash-equal) iff they were created from the same raw class and from bindings whose type-parameter sequences are pairwise equal; keys created from different parameter sequences for the same raw class, or from different raw classes, are unequal.

For a bean property with inclusion ALWAYS/NON_NULL/default where SerializationFeature.WRITE_EMPTY_JSON_ARRAYS is disabled, empty values are suppressed (via BeanPropertyWriter.MARKER_FOR_EMPTY) when the property's effective serialization type — the type after refinement by @JsonSerialize(as=...) annotation override or static typing — is a container type, even if the property's declared field type is not itself a container type.

Deserializing a Locale String whose components are separated by hyphens at both boundaries — e.g. a string with two hyphens like "en-US-foo"/hyphen variant strings — yields a three-component Locale (language, country, variant), mirroring how a two-underscore string is parsed.

JavaType.withHandlersFrom(JavaType src) returns a JavaType that carries the same own-level type handler and value handler as `src` when those differ from this type's own handlers: the returned type's getTypeHandler() equals src.getTypeHandler() and getValueHandler() equals src.getValueHandler().

For an ISO-8601 date-time with no explicit timezone indicator (reaching the branch that appends 'Z'), StdDateFormat pads the trailing time portion up to a full 12-character 'HH:mm:ss.SSS' so fully-normalized forms parse to the correct GMT instant: when less than three fractional-second digits follow full seconds, zeros are appended to reach three digits, and when the whole sub-millisecond/fraction tail is absent the literal '.000' is appended once before the 'Z'.

When a ValueInstantiator for a Collection returns true for canCreateUsingArrayDelegate() but getArrayDelegateType(config) returns null, collection deserialization setup aborts by throwing an IllegalArgumentException whose message starts with 'Invalid array-delegate-creator definition for ' and mentions both 'canCreateUsingArrayDelegate()' and 'null for 'getArrayDelegateType()''.

When a Reference's effective class (from _from, whether a Class value or an instance's runtime class) is an array type, the class-name segment rendered by getDescription() (and hence toString()) is the fully-qualified name of the array's innermost element/component class followed by one empty "[]" suffix per array dimension (e.g. an int[][].class reference yields "int[][]"; a String[].class reference yields "java.lang.String[]").

CreatorCollector.addPropertyCreator records the supplied property list as the property-based creator arguments only when the offered property-based creator is actually adopted for the property-based slot (i.e. it replaces/becomes the stored C_PROPS creator). If the offered property-based creator is rejected by verifyNonDup in favor of an already-registered property-based creator, the previously recorded property-based arguments are left unchanged rather than being overwritten by the rejected candidate's properties.

The JsonMappingException raised for the blocked type identifies the offending class and the reason, formatted as "Illegal type (TemplatesImpl) to deserialize: prevented for security reasons" where the parenthesized token is the actual simple class name of the blocked type.

collectAndResolveSubtypesByClass(MapperConfig, AnnotatedMember property, JavaType baseType) with a null `property` (and non-null baseType) does not fail: it skips collection of subtypes from the property's own declared subtype annotations and still produces the result based on registered types and base-type-hierarchy annotation-derived subtypes. (When a non-null baseType supplies the raw base class, a null property no longer triggers a NullPointerException at the property-subtypes step.)

In refineSerializationType for a map/map-like type, when the explicit @JsonSerialize.keyAs value Class forms a primitive/wrapper pair with the key type's raw class (and is otherwise unrelated by inheritance), refinement must NOT throw a JsonMappingException; instead it must succeed, keeping the key's raw class and the returned map-like JavaType with the key's static typing forced.

The date-format list exposed in the ParseException message thrown when parsing fails (built from ALL_FORMATS) now includes the additional timezone-less ISO-8601 format string 'yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'.

When a class supplied in the parameterClasses varargs of constructParametricType is itself a generic type whose hierarchy resolution needs to walk its type variables, that parameter class is now resolved with empty (non-null) type bindings and must not throw a NullPointerException from unbound type-variable resolution (previously it was resolved with null bindings).

For an element whose content after its (possibly empty) attribute list consists of non-whitespace character/CDATA text immediately followed by a nested START_ELEMENT (true mixed content), XmlTokenStream returns the collected text as an XML_TEXT token — with that text exposed via getText() — rather than discarding the text and jumping straight to the nested element.
When the InputStream argument is null, writeBinary writes a null value (the empty/self-closing element appropriate to the current context) and returns 0.
A `:not(...)` selector whose parenthesized subselect is empty is rejected with an exception (the empty-argument case does not silently return the full result set).

In Whitelist URL-attribute protocol validation (method testValidProtocol), when el.absUrl resolves to an empty string (the value could not be made absolute, e.g. unknown/custom scheme with no resolvable base), the attribute's own original value is used as the basis for the allowed-protocol prefix check instead of the empty string, so a link or URL attribute value that cannot be absolutized is not rejected (dropped as unsafe) for that reason alone — it is validated by its as-written value.

Cleaning a source body whose element content is nested deeply (deep enough that the previous recursive cleaner overflowed the call stack) no longer throws StackOverflowError: Cleaner.clean(Document) and Cleaner.isValid(Document) complete on such deeply nested content instead of crashing.

In parseByteData charset auto-detection (charsetName argument null), when the selected first meta carries an http-equiv attribute whose content does not resolve to a charset via getCharsetFromContentType, and the same meta also has a charset attribute naming a supported charset (that does not throw IllegalCharsetNameException on the support check), that charset-attribute value is used to re-decode the document instead of keeping the initial default-UTF-8 decoding; an unsupported or illegal-name charset attribute is ignored and the default decoding is retained.

When escaping with OutputSettings escape mode set to xhtml, a non-breaking space character (U+00A0) is emitted as the literal text ' ' (hex numeric character reference), rather than being appended as the raw U+00A0 character. This applies both in text-node and in-attribute escaping (the U+00A0 case is not guarded by the inAttribute flag).
When a start tag contains unrecognized input that yields an empty attribute key AND an empty attribute value (e.g. stray punctuation such as '

When the byte stream passed to DataUtil.parseByteData begins with a UTF-32 byte-order-mark (big-endian bytes 00 00 FE FF, or little-endian bytes FF FE 00 00), the content is decoded using the UTF-32 charset, this BOM override taking precedence over any explicitly supplied charsetName or any meta-tag-detected charset, so the parsing is performed on correctly decoded text.

XmlDeclaration.outerHtml()/toString() serializes the node as a complete, well-formed declaration: the opening prefix ('?' for an XML declaration where isProcessingInstruction is false, '!' where true), the declaration name, every attribute currently stored on the node (each emitted in insertion order by the standard attribute HTML serializer), then the matching closing prefix followed by '>'. Thus an xml declaration with attributes version, encoding and an extra custom attribute round-trips as e.g. '<?xml version="1" encoding="UTF-8" something="else"?>' (all attributes preserved, trailing '?' emitted); a node with no attributes renders as '<?xml?>' and not as the pre-fix malformed '<?xml>' that omitted the trailing marker.

When the tokeniser parses a doctype declaration whose after-name keyword is PUBLIC or SYSTEM (matched case-insensitively), the resulting Token.Doctype records that keyword as the canonical uppercase string "PUBLIC" or "SYSTEM" respectively, and getPubSysKey() returns it; when a doctype declares neither keyword (e.g. bare <!DOCTYPE html>), getPubSysKey() returns null.

TokenQueue.chompBalanced(open, close) no longer silently returns the partially-consumed content when it reaches the end of the character queue before the nested delimiter group has been brought back into balance (depth > 0): it now fails by throwing an IllegalArgumentException instead of returning normally.

For self-closing start tags of the InBody rawtext elements (<noembed />, <iframe />, <xmp />) that reach handleRawtext, the tokenising mode used for the remainder of the document is the normal Data mode (not Rawtext), i.e. content and tags following such an element are not absorbed as raw element data by the closed element.

When the parser is building a table section element (tbody, thead, or tfoot) - i.e. active/open-element context is within that table body, and a '<template>' start tag is parsed - the template element is inserted at the current position as a child of the section element that is currently open (and pushed onto the open-element stack without transitioning out), rather than being treated as non-table content and fostered out ahead of the table.

After an Element is cloned via clone(), a subsequent structural mutation of the clone's child-node list (for example appending a new descendant/sibling element) must invalidate and refresh the clone's own cached shadow child-elements list, so that element-tree queries that depend on that cache (e.g. nextElementSibling, previousElementSibling, children of the affected element) on the clone reflect the new child — behaving for later mutation queries the same as an equivalent independently-built element would.

After Document.normalise() runs on a document that contains more than one head element, all head elements except the first one in document order are removed and their child nodes are moved into that first, surviving head element, leaving exactly one head.

A LeafNode (e.g. a TextNode or other leaf) now behaves as a node with zero child nodes for every Node operation that queries or traverses child nodes: child-enumeration operations that previously raised UnsupportedOperationException ('Leaf Nodes do not have child nodes.') from ensureChildNodes() now return/act on an empty child-node list instead — concretely childNodes() and childNodesCopy() return an empty list, childNode(index) accesses an empty list, and unwrap()/childNodesAsArray() treat the leaf as having no children rather than throwing.

When DataUtil.parseInputStream is given a null charset, finds no BOM and no <meta> charset, and the first child node of the resulting first-pass UTF-8-parsed document is a Comment whose data constitutes an XML declaration (i.e. it passes Comment.isXmlDeclaration) that names 'xml' and carries an 'encoding' attribute — the situation arising when the HTML parser tokenizes a leading <?xml version="..." encoding="X"?> prolog as a Comment rather than directly as an XmlDeclaration — the foundCharset is set from that declaration's encoding attribute, so the full stream is re-decoded using charset X (mirroring the behavior already present when that first child is a genuine XmlDeclaration). Observable upshot: e.g. Jsoup.parse(stream of bytes in iso-8859-1 beginning with <?xml version="1.0" encoding="iso-8859-1"?>, null, uri) yields a Document whose text content is decoded with iso-8859-1 rather than the default charset.

Attribute.getValue() returns an empty string ("") rather than null when the attribute's stored value is null (as for a boolean attribute such as "hidden" parsed from HTML). Non-null values are returned unchanged.

Adding a header (via header/addHeader, which routes values through fixHeaderEncoding/looksLikeUtf8) whose ISO-8859-1 byte form ends with an incomplete UTF-8 multi-byte sequence whose continuation range reaches or exceeds the end of the data no longer throws an out-of-bounds exception; instead the value is accepted and stored unchanged (i.e., not treated as valid-looking UTF-8 and therefore not re-decoded to UTF-8).

Constructing a CharacterReader (via any of its constructors, since all delegate to CharacterReader(Reader, int) after the initial buffer-up) over input whose initially-buffered content contains 10 or more NUL ('\0') characters throws an UncheckedIOException with message "Input is binary and unsupported".

FormElement.formData() excludes a form control element from the returned key/value data when the element's type attribute is "button" (case-insensitively, e.g. "BUTTON"), even if that element is otherwise form-submittable, enabled, and named.

In CoreOperationRelationalExpression.compute(Object left, Object right), when after reduction left is NOT an Iterator but right IS an Iterator, the operation's result is true iff the actual relational comparison (e.g. <, <=, >, >= as given by the operation's evaluateCompare) holds between the (non-iterator) left operand as the FIRST relation argument and at least one element yielded by the right iterator as the SECOND argument; otherwise the result is false (the operand order is no longer reversed).

When the right operand of an "=" / "!=" comparison (CoreOperationCompare.equal) evaluates to an InitialContext EvalContext, it is no longer collapsed to that context's single node pointer; instead the context is left in place (reset) so that the comparison iterates over the nodes the InitialContext selects, returning a match if any individual selected node value equals the left operand — e.g. a right variable holding a whole-collection/array is decomposed element by element rather than its composite value being compared wholesale against the left side.

When a non-null chars array is supplied to RandomStringUtils.random with start==0 and end==0, the generated string's characters are drawn only from within that chars array (index range [0, chars.length)); in particular this no longer overflows the array bounds (previously could select arbitrary near-Integer.MAX_VALUE indices causing ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException), and with a single-element chars set the deterministic result is the repeated char regardless of the letters/numbers flags.

The integer returned by translate is the number of input characters consumed, counting the optional terminating ';' only when a ';' immediately follows the consumed numeric digits: for an unterminated entity (no semicolon) the returned count omits the formerly-always-added 1, so e.g. a standalone '&#NNN' at end-of-input returns exactly its own full length; for a semicolon-terminated entity the semicolon is counted so the return is unchanged from before.

NumberUtils.createNumber rejects as invalid any input containing a '.' in which the exponent-marker position expPos (= str.indexOf('e') + str.indexOf('E') + 1) falls after the decimal point but exceeds the string's length (so expPos is not before decPos yet still past the end) by throwing NumberFormatException with message str + " is not a valid number." rather than throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException from str.substring(decPos+1, expPos).

indexOfAny(CharSequence, char[]) does not report a hit at the position of a cs character that is only a code-unit match: when cs's char at i is a high surrogate at a non-terminal cs position whose matching char in searchChars is a high surrogate at a non-terminal search position, indexOfAny returns i (the high surrogate's index) only if the immediately following code unit in cs equals the immediately following code unit in searchChars (i.e. the same supplementary character); otherwise it continues searching past i.
escapeJava(Writer, String) writes a forward-slash character to the Writer as a bare '/' and does not emit a preceding backslash for it.

escapeJava(String) and escapeJava(Writer,String) escape each literal forward-slash character '/' in the printable-ASCII position of the input by writing the two characters backslash then slash ("\/") rather than outputting the slash bare (the new case is not gated on the escape-SingleQuote flag).

As a result of the carry being keyed to real month lengths, a period spanning one or more complete calendar months (whose months may have differing/less-than-31 day counts) resolves into whole months plus a residual day count that is a genuine leftover within a real month, and is no longer further perturbed by a post-pass that re-normalized every field estimate by subtracting a reduceAndCorrect correction (those calls and the reduceAndCorrect helper have been removed).

When the argument to compareTo is of a different runtime class whose binary name differs from the receiver's runtime class name (a genuinely different enum type), ValuedEnum.compareTo throws a ClassCastException whose message is "Different enum class '<short class name of other's class>'" rather than returning a value.

When the pattern of a newly built FastDateParser cannot be fully consumed by the format-field grammar (i.e. trailing pattern text — such as an unterminated single-quoted literal — remains unconsumed after tokenization), constructing the parser throws IllegalArgumentException (reporting that parsing 'Failed to parse' the pattern and the index where it gave up) rather than silently building a parser for the partially-consumed pattern.

After DSCompiler.atan2(y, yOffset, x, xOffset, result, resultOffset) returns, the 0th-order (value) element result[resultOffset] is set to FastMath.atan2(y[yOffset], x[xOffset]) for every input, thereby yielding the IEEE atan2 value in the special cases (+0/+0, +0/-0, -0/+0, -0/-0, and ±infinity combinations) where the branch-based derivative value computation produces an incorrect or NaN result.

guessParametersErrors throws an EstimationException for insufficient degrees of freedom (message reporting the parameter count) if and only if the number of measurements is less than or equal to the number of unbound parameters of the problem.

In AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer the square-root matrix of a DiagonalMatrix weight (as surfaced by getWeightSquareRoot()) is itself produced as a DiagonalMatrix whose (i,i) entry equals FastMath.sqrt of the corresponding input diagonal entry, computed directly along the diagonal rather than via EigenDecomposition; for a non-diagonal weight matrix the general (EigenDecomposition-based) square root continues to apply.

The NumberIsTooLargeException thrown by the boundary range-overflow guard reports the overflowing upper-bound value with an OVERFLOW message in its exception context and an INDEX message identifying the coordinate (dimension) whose upper−lower range overflowed.

When a user-supplied convergence checker reports convergence during an iteration, doOptimize returns the best point (per goal) among the initial guess and every trial point evaluated across all iterations up to and including the current one — i.e. the globally best point encountered, not merely the better of the last two consecutive points (current/previous).

When an optimization terminates because the user-supplied ConvergenceChecker reports convergence during doOptimize, the returned point (result of optimize) is the better of the two most recently evaluated points (`current` and `previous`) according to the goal type — the one with the lower objective value when the goal is MINIMIZE, and the higher when the goal is MAXIMIZE — rather than unconditionally the most recently evaluated/latest point.

In computeGeometricalProperties, when getVertices() returns an empty loop array (v.length == 0), the region is reported as covering the whole space (getSize() = POSITIVE_INFINITY, barycenter = NaN) only if the underlying BSP tree has no cut (getTree(false).getCut() == null) and its root attribute is TRUE; in every other empty-loop case — including a degenerate/empty region whose BSP tree still has a cut node — getSize() is 0 and the barycenter is Vector2D(0,0).

During backward integration (target t before the current step start), in every trial-step attempt inside the local-error control loop, the step size is clamped so that the step never extends below the integration target: if stepStart + stepSize <= t, the step size is reduced to t - stepStart. As a consequence, no intermediate derivative evaluation for that trial step occurs at a time before t.

In the solution point returned by SimplexTableau.getSolution(), an original decision variable whose tableau column is basic in the objective-function row (tableau row 0) is reported with value 0 — rather than being read from that row's RHS — regardless of the objective row's right-hand-side entry and regardless of the negative-variable ('x-') shift term used for unrestricted decision variables.

When, during acceptance of one integrator step that had multiple event handlers scheduled to occur (pending) inside it, the chronologically-first event's handler requests STOP so that acceptStep copies its interpolated state into y and returns that event's time early having marked the step as last, every other event handler that was also scheduled to occur later within the same candidate step is notified via stepAccepted at that same event time (with the copied state) before acceptStep returns, so none of the remaining handlers is left stepping from stale (pre-event) bracketing state.

ebeDivide(RealVector v) computes, for every index i at which `this` holds a non-default entry, the quotient this[i]/v[i] into a freshly created result OpenMapRealVector, and returns it; when such a quotient falls within this vector's zero-tolerance epsilon it is dropped as a default entry, and this drop must not cause later source entries to be skipped or the call to abort with a concurrent-modification exception during iteration.

When a Regula Falsi solver (Method.REGULA_FALSI) reaches an iteration in which the computed secant approximation coincides with the current upper endpoint x == x1 (so the plain false-position update would make no progress), the solver displaces the lower endpoint x0 inward toward x1 (to a point inside [x0, x1]) and recomputes the function value there, so the bracket shrinks and the iteration can continue; consequently a regula falsi solve does not stall indefinitely with the endpoint x1 fixed and, given bracketing and sufficient evaluations, converges to the root rather than cycling or exhausting the evaluation budget at a repeat of x1.

Vector3D.crossProduct returns Vector3D.ZERO (the null vector (0,0,0), without throwing) whenever the product of the two operands' squared norms (v1.getNormSq() * v2.getNormSq()) falls below the numerical-safety threshold MathUtils.SAFE_MIN, i.e. when one or both input vectors are of subnormally-small magnitude so that the naive computation would underflow or suffer catastrophic loss.

A BaseOptimizer constructs its inherited iterations Incrementor with an initial maximal count of Integer.MAX_VALUE (rather than 0), so that getMaxIterations() reports Integer.MAX_VALUE when no MaxIter option is supplied and subclasses may call incrementIterationCount() without triggering a TooManyIterationsException solely for lack of a configured MaxIter.

When a non-null VectorialConvergenceChecker is configured, doOptimize evaluates checker.converged against the last accepted trial's pair only (inside the successful-iteration branch), and applies no convergence-checker return on rejected probes; the checker is therefore never consulted about a rejected candidate.
After constructing with the no-arg constructor, getMaxEvaluations() returns 1000.

The stop condition evaluated when processing a firing event is the disjunction (OR) of stop() across all registered event states at that event time, not just the currently firing state: if any handler requests stopping when its state is advanced to the event time, isLastStep becomes true and the integration terminates at that event time.

For an m×n input matrix with m<n whose compact/truncated SVD retains a positive-singular-value count p strictly less than m (rank deficiency or explicit truncation via constructor max), getV() returns an n×p right-singular factor computed from the full m-row eigenvector submatrix, so that when no truncation was applied the product getU()*getS()*getVT() recomposes the original matrix to within floating-point tolerance (instead of the last retained V column being computed without its secondary-bidiagonal coupling term and thereby causing the recomposition to diverge from the input).

UnivariateRealSolverUtils.bracket(function, initial, lowerBound, upperBound, maximumIterations) treats an expanded interval [a,b] on which f(a)*f(b) == 0.0 (i.e. at least one endpoint value is exactly zero) as a successful bracketing and returns the two-element array {a, b}, instead of throwing ConvergenceException.

Line.revert() returns a Line whose point closest to the origin (getOrigin()/zero) is unchanged from the receiver's — the reverted line lies on the same geometric line and reverses only the orientation, preserving the receiver's closest-to-origin point exactly rather than recomputing it.

For 0 <= n <= 20 MathUtils.factorialLog(n) returns the natural logarithm of the exact factorial (equal to Math.log of the exact n! value), rather than a value obtained by summing individual Math.log terms.
DelegatingMethod.hashCode() returns the hash code of the wrapped java.lang.reflect.Method (rather than a constant), keeping it consistent with equals between equal DelegatingMethods.

A deep-stub mock newly created as a method-call return value through ReturnsDeepStubs is Serializable (its creation settings include serializable()), so that mock object alone can be serialized and deserialized.

When the Same matcher's wanted value is null, the token written into the description in the position of the wanted value (between the '(' and ')' in the 'same(...)' text) is the literal string "null".

When SpyAnnotationEngine.process encounters a @Spy-annotated field whose value is a non-null instance that is not already a mock, it replaces the field value with a Mockito mock whose configured mock name is the field's own name, so that the created spy is referred to by that field name (e.g. in Mockito error/verification messages that print the mock's name) rather than by a generated default mock name.

In comparing an argument against a matcher's string description (the toStringEquals path used for suspicious-argument detection), a null argument does not throw a NullPointerException: the null argument is treated as having the string representation "null", so a matcher whose StringDescription is the literal string "null" is considered to have an equal string representation.

During VerificationOverTimeImpl.verify's polling loop, an AssertionError thrown by delegate.verify(data) that is NOT a MockitoAssertionError (e.g. a plain java.lang.AssertionError or any AssertionError subtype other than MockitoAssertionError and the JUnit-flavoured ArgumentsAreDifferent) is no longer allowed to propagate immediately out of verify; it is now passed to handleVerifyException and thereby subjected to the recoverability/retry logic — i.e. stored as the accumulated error and, if the delegate can recover, slept/retried until the timer elapses (only then rethrown), rather than escaping from the very first polling iteration it occurs in.

When ZoneInfoCompiler.verbose() is called on a thread that has never previously stored a value in the cVerbose thread-local (i.e. no prior ThreadLocal.set on that thread), it returns false instead of throwing a NullPointerException as a result of the underlying thread-local value being null.

calculatePrintedLength for a SECONDS_MILLIS or SECONDS_OPTIONAL_MILLIS field returns a length that reflects the extra minus sign that printTo(StringBuffer,...) emits for a negative combined value (i.e. it uses a one-larger baseline for negative combined values than for non-negative ones), so the computed printed length matches the actual emitted string length, including for the negative-sub-second case.

When computeMillis is invoked with resetFields=true on a bucket holding two or more saved fields, the returned instant is computed so that, after the saved fields have been applied in priority (sorted) order with round-floor resetting, they are applied a second time with reset/round-floor applied only to the last (highest-priority/smallest) saved field; consequently any finer field detail that an intermediate applied field's round-floor in the first pass would otherwise have discarded above the last field is recovered, so the returned millis reflects all saved field values consistently. (With resetFields=false, or a single saved field, the re-pass leaves the result unchanged.)
MutableDateTime.addWeekyears(0) leaves the instant (getMillis) unchanged, i.e. adding zero weekyears is an observable no-op.

GJChronology.getInstance(zone, gregorianCutover, minDaysInFirstWeek) throws IllegalArgumentException when a non-null gregorianCutover resolves (in the target time zone, interpreted on the Gregorian calendar) to a date whose proleptic year is <= 0 — i.e. a cutover on or before 0001-01-01, such as LocalDate(-2,6,30) — so that no GJ chronology can be created whose cutover falls at or before Gregorian year zero. (Calling with a null cutover, which selects the default 1582 cutover, is unaffected.)

DateTimeZone.forOffsetMillis(int millisOffset) throws IllegalArgumentException (whose message includes the offending value) when millisOffset is outside the closed interval from -86,399,999 ms (-23:59:59.999) to +86,399,999 ms (+23:59:59.999), i.e. whenever its magnitude is at least a full day (86,400,000 ms); in-range millis offsets still resolve to the corresponding fixed-offset zone.

get_write_function(output), when output is a str or a pycompat.PathLike, returns a callable that appends each string it is called with to a file opened at the path given by the output argument itself (rather than at the undefined name output_path, which raised NameError before the fix).

The AnsibleError raised for an installed collection directory lacking MANIFEST.json has a message that includes the collection name and states that a MANIFEST.json is expected if the collection has been built and installed via ansible-galaxy.

When state is present and want['text'] differs from have's text, map_obj_to_commands builds the banner command using want['text'] with leading/trailing newline characters removed but all other surrounding whitespace (spaces, tabs) preserved.
The env lookup resolves environment variable values from the controller process's ambient environment, using ansible.utils.py3compat.environ as the environment mapping.

For a collection requirement string whose parsed URL scheme is a non-empty value other than http/https (case-insensitive), _get_collection_info does NOT attempt a download; it takes the collection-name path instead (validating the name as a collection name).

Changing the vrf to a non-default value on an unconfigured device yields commands ['management api http-commands', 'no shutdown', 'vrf <vrf>', 'no shutdown'] (state command appears both before and after the vrf command).

LinuxHardware._replace_octal_escapes(value) returns the given string with every backslash-prefixed three-decimal-digit sequence (e.g. \040) replaced by the character whose value is that sequence interpreted in base 8 (\040 -> space), and leaves all other characters (including a backslash that is not followed by exactly three digits, and any shorter/longer digit run) unchanged.

GalaxyCLI.init_parser passes the description "Perform various Role and Collection related operations." to the superclass init_parser, so the ansible-galaxy CLI's top-level help/usage description mentions both Role and Collection operations.
The `collections` FieldAttribute of CollectionSearch is marked as a static attribute, so it is never templated during post-validation; the value is used as-is.

When check_required_arguments finds one or more required parameters missing, the raised TypeError's message lists the missing parameter names in sorted (lexicographic) order (e.g. 'missing required arguments: a, b, c').

CollectionRequirement._meets_requirements treats a requirement (in any form, including an operator form such as '>=0.0.1') against an installed version of '*' as satisfied — it skips that requirement rather than attempting a version comparison — when a parent is set and the requirement is not itself '*'.
The cleanup path of `black.reformat_many` calls `executor.shutdown()` only when `executor is not None`, so a run that fell back to a `None` executor does not raise `AttributeError` during cleanup.
In Driver._partially_consume_prefix, a tab character in the prefix advances the tracked indentation column by exactly 1, i.e. a tab is counted the same as a space rather than as 4 columns.

The async-def state used for async/await tokenization is only entered when the stashed `async` is immediately followed by `def`; an `async for` does not enable that state (so subsequent `async`/`await` occurrences outside an `async def` are not tokenized as ASYNC/AWAIT).

get_future_imports returns the original (unaliased) module name for a future import written with a single `as` alias, e.g. `from __future__ import unicode_literals as _unicode_literals` yields a set containing `"unicode_literals"` (and not `"_unicode_literals"`), rather than raising/asserting.

EmptyLineTracker.maybe_empty_lines returns 0 blank lines before a decorator line when the immediately preceding emitted line is a standalone comment line (i.e., a line consisting of a single STANDALONE_COMMENT leaf), regardless of the decorator's indentation depth.

The `--- (original)` and `+++ (formatted)` labels produced by `format_file_in_place` in DIFF mode preserve the path spelling the caller passed in (e.g. a relative path stays relative), since the path is not resolved before being formatted into the diff headers.

When the platform default encoding differs from UTF-8, the temporary log file produced by black.dump_to_file contains the dumped text encoded as UTF-8 bytes rather than in the platform default encoding.

The `--config PATH` option of the black CLI requires PATH to point to an existing file: passing a --config value that does not exist is rejected as an invalid parameter (usage error) before any configuration-reading callback runs.

EmptyLineTracker.maybe_empty_lines returns a `before` count of 0 for the first line it is asked about (i.e. when it has not yet processed any line, so `previous_line is None`), so no empty lines are emitted at the beginning of the formatted file even if the newline count of the first line's first leaf prefix (or any other part of the computation) would otherwise yield a positive count.

The decision to wrap the first testlist_star_expr child in invisible parentheses is triggered by the child's position (index 0) and node type, independent of whether the previous leaf's value was in parens_after, so a statement like `a, b = ...` (with no preceding assignment leaf marker) still gets its tuple target wrapped.

When bracket_split_build_line builds the body of a split import line (is_body=True and original.is_import) and none of the leaves is a COMMA, a comma leaf is inserted immediately after the last leaf that is not a STANDALONE_COMMENT, so the comma always precedes any trailing standalone-comment leaves (a comma is never placed after a standalone comment / at the very end of the list when a trailing standalone comment exists).

get_grammars(target_versions) with a non-empty target_versions set that contains at least one Python 2 version (e.g. {TargetVersion.PY27}) returns a list of exactly two grammars, in the order (python_grammar_no_print_statement, python_grammar) — i.e. the Python 3-style no-print-statement grammar is attempted first and the full Python 2 grammar second.

find_hook returns a list of absolute paths to ALL valid hook scripts matching the requested hook name (e.g. both pre_gen_project.py and pre_gen_project.sh are included when both exist), rather than only the first match.
cookiecutter.exceptions defines a FailedHookException class that subclasses CookiecutterException, so it can be imported and caught by name.
APIRouter.include_router propagates each included APIRoute's response_model_exclude_defaults and response_model_exclude_none values to the newly created route.

is_scalar_field returns False for a field that satisfies the base scalar conditions (shape is SINGLETON, type is not a BaseModel subclass, type is not a sequence/collection/dict type, and the field schema is not a params.Body) whenever the field has sub_fields and at least one of those sub_fields is not itself scalar.

jsonable_encoder, when given a pydantic BaseModel whose Config does not define a `json_encoders` attribute, does not raise AttributeError but instead encodes the model by falling back to the caller-supplied `custom_encoder`.

_prepare_response_content recurses into list values, returning a new list in which each element has been prepared, so BaseModels nested inside a list response are also converted (with aliases / exclude_unset applied) rather than being passed through as model instances.

When multiple collected parameters share the same name, the entry kept is the last one encountered in the collected parameter order (its 'in', 'required', 'schema', 'description' and 'deprecated' fields win), rather than the first.
Calling update(x, new_x) returns a tensor whose value is the updated value of variable x (i.e. new_x when evaluated), rather than the raw assign op object.

Sequential.get_config() includes a 'build_input_shape' entry equal to the input_shape value that was passed to build() when the model was built from an explicit shape, and omits the 'build_input_shape' entry entirely when no such shape was ever recorded (e.g. a freshly constructed model, or one built only via a first-layer batch_input_shape).
keras.backend.numpy_backend defines a public module-level function in_top_k(predictions, targets, k) (previously absent from the numpy backend).

Bidirectional.get_updates_for(inputs) returns the concatenation of the Bidirectional layer's own updates (registered on itself for the given inputs, via Layer.get_updates_for), the forward_layer's updates for those inputs, and the backward_layer's updates for those inputs; previously the wrapper's inherited implementation consulted only the originally passed layer, so the forward/backward sublayers' updates never appeared.
Constructing a TimeseriesGenerator with a start_index+length that exceeds end_index (the effective start_index is greater than end_index) raises a ValueError; otherwise construction succeeds.
ReduceLROnPlateau's constructor accepts a keyword argument named `min_delta` (default 1e-4) in place of the former `epsilon` argument, so `epsilon` is no longer a named parameter of the signature.

On Python 3, text_to_word_sequence replaces every character in `filters` with the full `split` string before splitting, so that when `split` is multi-character the filtered characters are substituted by the whole split string, not by individual characters.

ImageDataGenerator.standardize no longer applies the generator's preprocessing_function to its input; standardize only performs rescaling/normalization (rescale, samplewise/featurewise center and std normalization, zca whitening) on the input it is given.

MetricsHandler.get invokes configure_http_handler on the metrics collector object (the value of self._scheduler._state._metrics_collector) passing the handler itself, rather than invoking it on the object returned by generate_latest().

SimpleTaskState.get_necessary_tasks excludes tasks in UNKNOWN status from the returned necessary set: an UNKNOWN-status task with scheduler_disable_time None contributes neither its own id nor its deps, exactly as DONE and DISABLED tasks are excluded.

CentralPlannerScheduler.prune() invokes SimpleTaskState.prune on every active task on each call, regardless of whether the task is in necessary_tasks, so prune's state side effects (FAILED->PENDING retry reset when retry delay has elapsed, DISABLED re-enable when disable_persist has elapsed, and stamping task.remove when a task has no stakeholders) are applied to necessary tasks too.

Instantiating a concrete BeamDataflowJobTask subclass whose dataflow_params is a DataflowParamKeys instance also runs the luigi.Task constructor (super().__init__()), so the constructed task is a fully initialized luigi.Task (e.g. task_id/task_family are populated) rather than a task on which luigi.Task.__init__ was never called.

Task.to_str_params() returns a dict containing an entry for every parameter the task was constructed with, including parameters declared with significant=False; no parameter is omitted on the basis of its significance.
luigi.interface.run called without an explicit cmdline_args argument (cmdline_args is None) does not raise an error and instead proceeds using sys.argv[1:] as the command-line arguments.
Constructing Worker(worker_id) without passing last_active results in worker.last_active being a numeric (float) epoch timestamp rather than None.
The scheduler config exposes a boolean parameter `prune_on_get_work` (accessibly as an attribute of the scheduler Config object) that defaults to False.

SparkSubmitTask._dict_arg, when given a name and a non-empty dict, emits for each key/value entry the pair [name, 'prop=value'] with the formatted 'prop=value' text carrying no surrounding double quotes (previously the value was wrapped as '"prop=value"').

S3CopyToTable.run() binds its local load path to the value of the s3_load_path attribute itself (via attribute access that does not invoke it as a callable), rather than to the result of calling s3_load_path.

When run_job is invoked without SSH configuration and the job's jar() returns a falsy value (e.g. None or ''), it raises HadoopJarJobError with the message "Jar not defined" instead of attempting to check the path, and never calls os.path.exists on the jar value.

Register.__get_reg()/Register.task_names() include every registered Task subclass regardless of whether it overrides run: a class whose run attribute is the inherited, non-overridden value is no longer omitted from the registry listing. Observable via task_names() listing such a class and get_task_cls(name) resolving it.

In the fallback (non-JSON) path, TupleParameter.parse returns tuple(literal_eval(x)), i.e. the ast.literal_eval result is coerced into a tuple, so any literal that evaluates to a non-tuple container (such as a bracketed list) is returned as a tuple rather than as that container type.

For an assistant calling get_work, RUNNING tasks whose capable-worker set is empty are excluded from the returned reply's 'running_tasks' list; RUNNING tasks with at least one capable worker remain included.

In Task.get_param_values, the ordered list of parameters that positional arguments are bound to consists of exactly the non-global parameters (params where is_global is False), in parameter-declaration order; global parameters are never bound from positional arguments regardless of their significant flag, and non-global parameters with significant=False are still positionally bindable.

_recursively_freeze converts a tuple value (and any tuple nested inside a Mapping or sequence) into a tuple of recursively-frozen elements, in the same way it already does for lists, rather than returning the tuple unchanged.

While a task's status is RUNNING or BATCH_RUNNING, a status update to DONE, FAILED, or RUNNING is applied only when the requesting worker equals the task's worker_running; in that case the task's status is updated (and the task history is written).
_partition_tasks records a set_tasks['ever_failed'] status containing every task that has a 'FAILED' entry in the worker's task history.

Axis.set_view_interval / Axis.set_data_interval (the setters generated by _make_getset_interval for XAxis and YAxis) called with ignore=False on an axis whose current interval in the shared axes Limits object is inverted (i.e. its first entry is not less than its second entry) store the new interval as exactly (max(vmin, vmax, oldmin), min(vmin, vmax, oldmin)), where (oldmin, oldmax) is the current interval; the first (upper) entry is therefore derived from the current interval's first entry, not its second entry.
Calling Axis.set_inverted on the base Axis class raises NotImplementedError (with message 'Derived must override') instead of modifying the view interval.

NDFrame.pct_change with freq=None does not apply the index-deduplication/reindex post-processing to the computed percentage change, so the returned object's index matches the (filled) input data's index exactly — including when that index contains duplicate labels, in which case no rows are dropped and no reindexing is attempted.
Categorical.min on an empty (zero-length) ordered Categorical returns the dtype's NA value (NaN) instead of raising an error or returning a category.

A float scalar .loc key on a CategoricalIndex whose categories are string/unicode/mixed is not rejected with a TypeError at the scalar-conversion step; the float key is passed through and the subsequent lookup of an absent label raises KeyError.

IntervalIndex.get_indexer accepts a CategoricalIndex as its target and returns, for each position of the categorical, the same indexer value that would be returned for the corresponding underlying value (i.e. get_indexer(categorical_target) is elementwise equal to get_indexer(target) where target is the categorical's values), regardless of whether the categorical is ordered or unordered.

Index.get_value raises InvalidIndexError(key) when the values of `series` are an ExtensionArray and `key` is not a scalar (e.g. an ndarray/list of labels), rather than falling through to a numpy-based lookup of the values.

For the non-scipy interpolation path of missing.interpolate_1d (method in {'linear', 'time', 'index', 'values'}), when the x-axis / index values are not monotonically increasing, the interpolated result is nonetheless the value defined by the valid (x, y) pairs treated as a sorted set of knots, rather than the (incorrect) result of passing the unsorted x-knots directly to np.interp. I.e. the each interpolated point equals the linear interpolation between the two valid x-knots that bracket it in sorted order, using the y-value belonging to each of those x-knots.

pandas.melt() does not raise a KeyError for value_vars labels that are present in the DataFrame when the value_vars labels and the frame's column labels have mixed types (e.g. an integer column name listed alongside string column names); the presence check compares labels without coercing them to a common (string) dtype.

GroupBy._reindex_output accepts an optional `fill_value` argument (default np.NaN) and uses that scalar as the fill value for entries created by the categorical-group-expansion reindex: in the as_index=True branch it is forwarded to `output.reindex`, and in the as_index=False branch it is forwarded to the `output.set_index(...).reindex(index, ...)` call.

ObjectBlock._replace_coerce, when the given boolean mask contains no True entries but convert is truthy, returns a single-element list containing the block converted via convert(numeric=False, copy=True) (rather than returning the unchanged block itself).

When a rejected dtype is passed, the raised exception is a ValueError whose message has the form "Incorrect `dtype` passed: expected <expected>, received <dtype>", where <expected> is 'signed integer' for Int64Index, 'unsigned integer' for UInt64Index, and 'float' for Float64Index.
Categorical.replace(to_replace, value, inplace=False) returns a new Categorical with the replacement applied when inplace is False, and returns None (mutating self in place) when inplace is True.

When several rows of the intermediate percentage-change result share the same index label, NDFrame.pct_change keeps the first such row for that label and discards the later ones (rather than raising or keeping all of them).

When a scalar np.datetime64 operand is subtracted from a timedelta64-dtype DatetimeLikeArrayMixin (e.g. `np.datetime64(t) - TimedeltaArray`/`TimedeltaIndex`), __rsub__ returns the result of `Timestamp(other) - self` (a datetime64-dtype array of Timestamps) rather than attempting to wrap the scalar in DatetimeArray; this holds for the scalar np.datetime64('NaT') as well, yielding all-NaT entries.

BinGrouper.recons_codes returns a list containing exactly one integer ndarray, whose value is 0 followed by every index i in the range 1 <= i < len(self.bins) for which self.bins[i] != self.bins[i-1], in ascending order (i.e. the positions of the non-empty (distinct) bin boundaries, always including position 0).
Series.var() on a timedelta64-dtype Series raises TypeError matching "operation 'var' not allowed" (for both empty and non-empty timedelta Series), instead of returning a Timedelta/NaT.

BaseGrouper.agg_series, when the fast aggregation path `_aggregate_series_fast(obj, func)` raises a TypeError whose message string contains the substring "ndarray", does not propagate that TypeError; instead it falls back to and returns the result of `self._aggregate_series_pure_python(obj, func)`.

Categorical.astype(dtype) where dtype is an extension-array dtype (i.e. is_extension_array_dtype(dtype) is True, and dtype is not categorical) returns a pandas array object whose dtype is exactly the requested extension dtype (e.g. an IntervalArray for IntervalDtype), holding the categorical's values in the categorical's order; it no longer falls through to np.array(self, dtype=dtype, copy=copy) and therefore no longer raises 'TypeError: data type not understood' for such dtypes.
_coerce_to_type casts boolean-dtype input to int64, so that boolean data reaching cut/qcut is treated as numeric 0/1 data instead of a bool array.

should_series_dispatch returns True when one of the two operands' first-column dtype is datetime64 and the other's first-column dtype is object, regardless of which operand holds the datetime64 dtype and which holds the object dtype (previously only the left-operand-datetime64 / right-operand-object ordering returned True).

When dispatch_to_series is called with `right` an ABCSeries whose dtype is exactly `timedelta64[ns]` and `axis == "columns"`, the per-column operand passed to `func` for column i is obtained from a numpy (positional) view of the Series rather than from `b.iloc[i]`, so that NaT entries retain timedelta semantics rather than datetime semantics.

When array_equivalent is called with strict_nan=True on object/string arrays and element-wise comparison raises a TypeError whose message contains "Cannot compare tz-naive", array_equivalent returns False (treats the arrays as not equivalent) instead of letting the TypeError propagate.

The TypeError raised by DatetimeTZDtype.construct_from_string for a matched-but-unconstructible string chains the underlying construction error as its __cause__ (err.__cause__ is the original KeyError/pytz.UnknownTimeZoneError, TypeError, or ValueError), rather than discarding it.
In apply_empty_result, the reduction-inference probe invokes the apply function with exactly one argument, an empty Series (Series([])), and no additional positional or keyword arguments.

Calling `_with_freq(freq)` on a TimedeltaArray/DatetimeArray returns a distinct array object (a view sharing the same underlying data) instead of mutating the receiver in place; the receiver's own `freq` is left unchanged by the call.

In array_equivalent's strict_nan=True branch for string/object dtypes, comparing two corresponding elements that are themselves array-like (e.g. lists/ndarrays held in an object array) no longer raises ValueError from an ambiguous truth value of a multi-element boolean array; the elementwise comparison is reduced to a single boolean before being used as a condition.

PandasArray.__setitem__(key, value) writes the value into the existing backing ndarray without changing the array's dtype: after any successful assignment self.dtype (and self._dtype) equals the dtype it had before the assignment; no upcasting to a wider result dtype occurs.

The freq assigned to an addition/subtraction result is determined from both the operand (`other`) and the actual result object produced by the underlying operation; `_get_addsub_freq` is invoked with the computed result so its dtype can be inspected.

For an operand that exposes a scalar `dtype` attribute (a numpy ndarray or a 1-D Series), _can_use_numexpr includes that operand's dtype name in the set of dtypes considered for the numexpr dtype-compatibility check, so that such an operand's dtype can cause the check to return False when the dtype is not in _ALLOWED_DTYPES[dtype_check].

_normalize raises ValueError with the message "<margins_name> not in pivoted DataFrame" when margins is True and the given margins label is neither a component of the last row's index name nor equal to the last column's label (i.e. the margins label is not positioned as the final row/column of the table).

DatetimeLikeArrayMixin.__add__ returns NotImplemented when other is a pandas Index (ABCIndexClass) instead of performing the operation itself, so the result is produced by the Index's reflected operation; concretely, for a TimedeltaArray tda, tda + dti equals tdi + dti for a DatetimeIndex dti = date_range('1999-12-31', periods=3), and tda + tdi equals tdi + tdi for a TimedeltaIndex tdi.
