_get_grouper's label/level ambiguity validation honors the groupby axis: when the key is found in the object and validate is True, obj._check_label_or_level_ambiguity is invoked with axis=axis (the axis passed to _get_grouper), so for axis=1 a key that is both a column-level name and an index label is reported as ambiguous.

For the empty-column-collection early return of DataFrame.quantile, the empty Index used for the result's column axis (the Series' index, or the DataFrame's columns) carries the name of the calling frame's columns axis, i.e. self.columns.name, and the result's axis labels are otherwise empty.

For a PeriodArray, _validate_insert_value's compatibility check raises IncompatibleFrequency (DIFFERENT_FREQ message) when the inserted Period's freq does not match the array's freq, rather than silently re-casting the Period to the array's freq.

Calling a rolling aggregation named 'skew' with a BaseIndexer subclass as the window (e.g. df.rolling(<BaseIndexer>).skew()) no longer raises NotImplementedError; 'skew' is treated as supported so the computation proceeds and returns a result.

Indexing with .loc using a 1-D list-like of scalar (non-tuple) labels against an axis whose labels are a MultiIndex resolves the labels against level 0 of that axis (a reindex-like multi-selection; for a Series/ndarray key it is the key's values, not its own index, that are used), and raises KeyError with a message containing 'not in index' when any requested label is not present, instead of silently ignoring the missing labels and returning only the rows/columns whose labels were found.

For a 1-dimensional object (ndim == 1), setting via `.at` with a tuple key of length greater than 1 assigns the value at that tuple label rather than raising: `series.at[1, 2] = 3` succeeds (and a subsequent `series.at[1, 2]` returns 3) for a Series with a single-level tuple-valued index, and `series.at[1, 3] = 5` succeeds for a Series with a two-level MultiIndex.

MonthOffset.apply_index returns a DatetimeIndex constructed from the shifted i8 values without passing the input index's freq (i.e. the input `i.freq` is not forwarded to `_simple_new`); only `dtype` is forwarded.

Calling validate_baseindexer_support with the function name "count" does not raise NotImplementedError (only names outside the supported set {count, min, max, mean, sum, median, std, var, kurt, quantile} raise NotImplementedError).
When DatetimeTimedeltaMixin.intersection returns the empty fast-path result (end < start), the result carries `self`'s freq (result.freq equals self.freq) rather than having a None freq.

DatetimeArray.tz_localize returns an array whose freq is None in the general case — i.e. for any call that is not one of: localizing to a UTC timezone, a length-1 array with a non-NaT value, or the tz=None-on-already-naive no-op. This includes localizing a multi-element tz-naive array to a non-UTC timezone (e.g. a 3-element daily range localized to 'US/Eastern' yields freq=None) and removing the timezone from a multi-element tz-aware array with tz_localize(None).

IntervalArray.__setitem__ raises a ValueError with the message "Cannot set float NaN to integer-backed IntervalArray" when assigning a scalar NA value (e.g. np.nan, None) to an IntervalArray whose subtype is integer (int*/uint*), and leaves the array unmodified in that case.
The TypeError raised by Series.to_timestamp for an unsupported index carries the message "unsupported Type <name>", where <name> is the type name of the series' index.

When every date-unit attempt for the data raises (TypeError, ValueError or OverflowError), _try_convert_to_date returns the original unmodified data together with a failure indicator (False), so the caller treats the data as not date-convertible.

GroupBy.quantile on a nullable integer extension-dtype column still infers an integer result, so with an interpolation other than 'linear'/'midpoint' the returned values are cast back to int64 (equivalently, output stays float for 'linear' and 'midpoint').

PeriodIndex._engine resolves its values from the index's underlying PeriodArray (self._values) rather than from the PeriodIndex object itself, so that the engine's value getter yields a PeriodArray (which exposes .view('i8') and .freq) instead of a PeriodIndex.

_wrap_inplace_method's generated in-place operators (__iadd__, __isub__, __imul__, __itruediv__, __ifloordiv__, __imod__, __ipow__, __iand__, __ior__, __ixor__) clear the operand's parent-cacher link (the attribute set via _set_as_cached) as part of the operation, so that after `s op= other` on a Series that was obtained as a cached column of a DataFrame, the parent DataFrame is NOT updated with the new Series data (i.e. a column previously dropped from the frame does not reappear).

assert_series_equal routes to the interval-specific comparison (assert_interval_array_equal on left.array/right.array) only when BOTH Series have interval dtypes; when exactly one Series has an interval dtype and the other does not, the interval branch is not taken and comparison falls through to a later dtype branch (ultimately the generic value comparison) instead of raising an 'Expected type IntervalArray' assertion from assert_interval_array_equal.

For a DataFrame-with-DataFrame flex arithmetic operation whose columns are not identical, when the operation is `**` (DataFrame.pow / DataFrame.__pow__) or the reversed `**` (DataFrame.rpow / DataFrame.__rpow__), the operation does NOT take the reindex-only-on-shared-columns path.

sanitize_array raises a TypeError with the message "Set type is unordered" when the data argument is a set (any collections.abc.Set instance, e.g. set or frozenset), instead of falling through to the catch-all cast path.

cartesian_product no longer coerces factors through pandas.core.common.values_from_object (the `import pandas.core.common as com` dependency is removed and the function still works for all supported inputs).

Assigning via .loc with a label indexer whose column part is a list-like containing labels not present in the columns, e.g. df.loc[:, ['a', 'newcol']] = values, no longer raises for the missing labels: the missing labels are first created as NaN-filled columns, and the assignment then proceeds normally.

When a CategoricalIndex is joined (Index.join via _join_monotonic or _join_non_unique) and the joined index is wrapped, the result is a CategoricalIndex whose dtype equals the calling index's dtype (same categories and orderedness), instead of a generic Index built from the raw joined values.
For a Series with a string ('abc') object index, ser.at[0] and ser.loc[0] raise KeyError matching '^0$' rather than a TypeError about label indexing.

The ValueError message raised by CategoricalDtype._from_values_or_dtype for an unrecognized non-string, non-CategoricalDtype `dtype` is f"Cannot not construct CategoricalDtype from {dtype}" (the repr of the offending dtype object interpolated into the message).

For a DataFrame with a non-unique info axis (duplicate columns), accessing an item by positional index via NDFrame._iget_item_cache returns the item at that position (through positional item slicing) instead of going through the take-with-is_copy path; the returned object is the column/Series at that integer position.

DataFrame._get_value(..., takeable=True) obtains its column Series through DataFrame._ixs(col, axis=1), so the retrieved column Series is the frame's cached column Series for that positional column (it is marked as cached against `self`, and is named after the column label).
Categorical.from_codes raises ValueError with message 'codes cannot contain NA values' when `codes` is an integer-typed extension array containing any NA (missing) value.

Series.__getitem__ with a non-scalar key that infers as integer-valued, when the Series index is not integer-, floating-, or IntervalIndex-typed, returns the same object as positional indexing with Series.iloc[key]: a Series whose values are taken by position and whose labels are the corresponding entries of self.index, rather than the result of the internal self._get_values(key) slice path (which could raise a slice-specific error or return a bare numpy array instead of a Series).
Block.setitem raises a ValueError when the passed indexer is an np.ndarray whose ndim exceeds the block's own ndim, instead of proceeding to attempt the assignment.

When `cols` is provided together with a list/tuple/ndarray/Index `header` of aliases, the length check compares the number of aliases against len(cols); writing succeeds iff len(header) == len(cols), and otherwise raises ValueError citing the cols-based column count.

When a TimeDeltaBlock's (or DatetimeBlock's) single stored value read by iget is an np.timedelta64 scalar, iget returns it wrapped as a pandas Timedelta instead of the raw np.timedelta64, representing the same duration.

When shift pads with the explicit Interval fill_value, only min(abs(periods), len(self)) pad entries are produced, so if abs(periods) exceeds len(self) the result length still equals len(self) and all entries equal fill_value.
The integer-extension-array handling in pandas.cut applies for all forms of bins: a scalar int, a sequence of bin edges, and an IntervalIndex all work with an integer-dtype extension array as x.

Because _convert_axes routes index/column axis data through the same _try_convert_data helper, reading a JSON document whose axis labels require an int64 coercion that overflows also returns a result instead of raising OverflowError.

A replace call on a block whose match mask is empty does not take an early no-op shortcut: Block.replace still produces its result through the putmask-based replacement path (and, when convert=True, the post-replacement convert step) rather than returning the original block/its copy.

The unstacked result of unstacking on a tuple-valued level name keeps the tuple names intact as level names: the levels that were not unstacked appear as the result's index name(s) and the unstacked tuple name appears as the name of the new column level (e.g., unstacking ("A", "a") from names [("A", "a"), ("B", "b")] yields an index named ("B", "b") and columns with a level named ("A", "a")).
The TypeError raised by pivot() for a missing/None `columns` argument has the message "pivot() missing 1 required argument: 'columns'".

Categorical.__contains__ returns self.isna().any() (i.e. True iff the Categorical contains at least one missing value) when key is a scalar NA value that is valid for the Categorical's categories dtype, as determined by is_valid_nat_for_dtype(key, self.categories.dtype); for example `np.nan in cat` is True exactly when the Categorical has any NaN value.
to_pickle accepts a generic filepath-or-buffer argument (str path, path-like object, URL, or file-like buffer) named filepath_or_buffer instead of requiring a plain path, resolving it before opening.

The TypeError raised by TimedeltaIndex.searchsorted for an incompatible value carries the message "searchsorted requires compatible dtype or scalar, not {type(value).__name__}" (the offending value's type name is interpolated).

PeriodIndex.searchsorted raises TypeError with a message containing "requires either a Period or PeriodArray" for any argument that is not a Period, NaT, str, or PeriodArray (e.g. an int64 ndarray, a timedelta64 array, a timedelta64 scalar, a datetime64 scalar).

Comparing a Period-backed array (PeriodArray / PeriodIndex / period-dtype Series) with an integer scalar no longer performs an element-wise comparison against a Period constructed from that integer and the array's freq; instead the integer scalar falls through the non-list-like path and yields an invalid-comparison result.

When a CustomBusinessHour offset is applied to a datetime (via BusinessHourMixin.apply) and the whole-business-day part bd is nonzero, the business days are skipped using the offset's own custom calendar (its weekmask, holidays, and calendar), so that dates falling on holidays or non-weekmask days are excluded from the day-skipping step; consequently the applied result advances only over valid custom business days when jumping whole business days.

For two fast-unionable TimedeltaIndex objects where self's first element is greater than other's first element, calling left.union(right, sort=False) returns an index whose values are self's values followed by exactly those values of other that are strictly less than self's first element (the overlap is removed), preserving the original element order rather than returning a sorted result.

AsyncioServer.start_serving() raises NotImplementedError when the delegated call self.server.start_serving() raises AttributeError (i.e., when the underlying server object lacks start_serving / does not support it).

For a Location header given as bytes that encode non-ASCII characters, the resulting redirected request URL percent-encodes those bytes using their raw byte values (so latin1-encoded '/ação' -> 'a%E7%E3o' and UTF-8-encoded '/ação' -> 'a%C3%A7%C3%A3o'), rather than percent-encoding UTF-8 of the latin1-decoded code points.

The ValueError message is exactly '<ClassName>.__init__() received both response and text', where <ClassName> is the runtime class whose __init__ was invoked (subclass-aware, e.g. 'Selector' for Selector and the subclass name for a subclass).
is_gzipped(response) matches the Content-Type value case-insensitively, so values such as 'Application/GZip' or 'APPLICATION/X-GZIP' return True.
response_status_message(status) returns a string of the form '<status> Unknown Status' when the status code has no entry in the HTTP reason-phrase mapping, instead of raising an exception.
WrappedRequest exposes a read-only attribute-style property 'host' that returns the netloc of the wrapped request's URL (same value as get_host()).
After a robots.txt download error for a netloc, RobotsTxtMiddleware leaves an entry for that netloc present in its parser cache (set to None) instead of deleting the cache entry.

A proxy CONNECT response delivered as a bytes object whose status line matches 'HTTP/1.x 200' is recognized by the response matcher, so the tunnel is established: the transport is switched to TLS and the endpoint's tunnel-ready deferred is called back with the protocol (instead of the match raising a str-pattern-on-bytes TypeError).

When FormRequest.from_response is called without an explicit url and the form has no 'action' attribute, the resulting request URL is the form's base URL resolved against the document base URL (i.e. the response URL, or the page's <base href> if present), rather than the raw action attribute.

When a `<name>_BASE` setting exists, `_getcomposite(name)` builds the composite from the `<name>_BASE` entries and from those entries of `self[name]` whose stored priority is strictly greater than the 'default' priority; entries of `self[name]` whose priority equals 'default' are NOT included in the returned composite even though they are present in `self[name]`.

In RedirectMiddleware.process_response, when the raw Location header value starts with '//' (a protocol-relative reference), the redirect target is resolved against the scheme of request.url rather than left to plain relative resolution: the Location value is rewritten to '<scheme-of-request.url>://<Location value with its leading slashes stripped>' before being urljoin-ed with request.url. Thus a request to 'http://example.com/a' with 'Location: //foo.com/path' redirects to 'http://foo.com/path', and an https request yields an 'https://...' target.

WrappedRequest.get_header returns the header value converted to a native string using error replacement, so a header value whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 yields a string with the undecodable bytes replaced (U+FFFD) instead of raising a UnicodeDecodeError.

CrawlerProcess.__init__ passes the instance's normalized settings object (self.settings, a Settings instance) to configure_logging, so that a falsy/empty dict argument does not cause the root-logger handler setup inside configure_logging to be skipped (and so configure_logging never receives a raw dict from CrawlerProcess).

scrapy.utils.log exposes a function failure_to_exc_info(failure) that, given a twisted.python.failure.Failure instance, returns the 3-tuple (failure.type, failure.value, failure.tb) suitable for use as a logging exc_info value.
create_instance raises a TypeError when the constructor chosen (from_crawler, from_settings, or the class itself) returns None, instead of returning None to the caller.

The deprecation warning emitted by Spider.start_requests is formatted to include, in '<module>.<classname>' form, the __module__ and __name__ of the concrete class of the spider instance on which start_requests() was called (i.e. the dynamic class, not always Spider).
The ValueError raised by Response.follow(None) is a plain ValueError (matching the check/raise semantics implemented in the patch).

ImagesPipeline.convert_image composites a palette-mode ('P') image over an opaque white background before converting it to RGB, rather than converting it directly to RGB, so that any transparency encoded in the palette is blended with white.
For a given pipeline component, values supplied as load-time overrides take precedence over the corresponding values found in meta['pipeline_args'][component_name] when both define the same key.

The local filter_spans defined in examples/information_extraction/entity_relations.py, when two overlapping input spans have the same length, keeps the span that starts at the smaller (earlier) token index rather than the later-starting one.
The Errors class exposes an error code attribute named E175, whose value is the message template "Can't remove rule for unknown match pattern ID: {key}".

spacy.errors.Warnings.W022 can be resolved (no AttributeError) and, through the @add_codes wrapper, resolves to the warning message '[W022] Training a new part-of-speech tagger using a model with no lemmatization rules or data. This means that the trained model may not be able to lemmatize correctly. If this is intentional or the language you're using doesn't have lemmatization data, you can ignore this warning by setting SPACY_WARNING_IGNORE=W022. If this is surprising, make sure you have the spacy-lookups-data package installed.'

In pip_unknown_command.get_new_command, the suggested command name is extracted from output text matching `maybe you meant "..."` by taking the entire quoted token (any characters except a double quote), so a suggestion containing non-[a-z] characters is captured in full rather than only its leading [a-z] prefix.

When get_new_command is called for a `man` command whose script contains neither '2' nor '3' and whose stderr does not indicate a missing manual entry, it returns a three-element list ordered as [man-3 variant, man-2 variant, last_arg + ' --help'], i.e. the last_arg --help suggestion comes last rather than first.

When the split command parts contain the standalone token '--set-upstream', git_push.get_new_command builds the corrected command from the command script with that token and the single token immediately following it removed.

Fish._get_overridden_aliases() returns a set of alias names (a Python set, not a list), so its result compares equal to a set literal of the same names and supports set semantics (e.g. `isinstance`/`type` check reports set).

For a git/hub command whose stderr contains the substring "did not match any file(s) known to git.", the git_add rule's match() returns True even if stderr does NOT contain "Did you forget to 'git add'?" (the modern-Git stderr form without the add hint).

sudo.match returns False for a command whose script starts with the token `sudo` (command.script_parts non-empty and command.script_parts[0] == 'sudo'), regardless of whether the command's stderr or stdout contains any of the permission-denied patterns that would otherwise cause a match.

get_all_executables splits the PATH environment variable using os.pathsep as the directory separator (rather than a hard-coded ':'), so on a platform whose os.pathsep is not ':' (e.g. Windows, where it is ';') a PATH value like 'C:\a;C:\b' is treated as two directory entries and the executables found in both directories are returned (instead of treating the whole string as one non-existent directory path).

dirty_unzip.get_new_command builds the corrected command as '<original script> -d <archive name without .zip>', shell-escaping that destination directory via shells.quote, so a directory name containing shell-special characters is emitted quoted and remains a single argument; for ordinary names the output is unchanged (e.g. 'unzip foo' -> 'unzip foo -d foo', 'unzip foo.zip' -> 'unzip foo.zip -d foo').

Iterating, calling len() on, or indexing (with any index, including out-of-range) a SortedCorrectedCommandsSequence constructed over an empty iterable completes without raising an exception, and iterating/len() report an empty result (list(seq) == [], len(seq) == 0).

The `cache`-decorated function (`thefuck.utils.cache`'s `_cache` wrapper) uses `contextlib.closing(shelve.open(cache_path))` as the `with` block's context manager, so the database returned by `shelve.open` is closed (its `close()` method called) when the cache read/write block exits, rather than requiring the shelve object itself to implement the context-manager protocol.

repr(CorrectedCommand(script, side_effect, priority)) produces the string 'CorrectedCommand(script={script}, side_effect={side_effect}, priority={priority})' with the three attribute values interpolated.

When the script contains no machine token (fewer than 3 space-separated tokens), get_new_command returns a single combined shell command joining 'vagrant up' with the original command, i.e. 'vagrant up && <original script>' without a trailing space before the separator.

When the script uses a longer launcher accepted by match ('xdg-open', 'gnome-open', 'kde-open'), get_new_command preserves that launcher verbatim and inserts 'http://' after it, e.g. 'xdg-open github.com' yields 'xdg-open http://github.com' (the launcher is not truncated or rewritten to 'open').

fix_file.get_new_command accepts settings that provide the customizable keys `fixlinecmd` and `fixcolcmd`, defaulting to `'{editor} {file} +{line}'` and `None` respectively when the caller does not supply them.

Settings.update(**kwargs) returns a new settings object in which, for any key present in both the receiver and kwargs, the receiver's existing value is retained and the kwargs value is ignored; calling Settings({'key': 'val'}).update(key='new-val') yields a result whose 'key' attribute equals 'val'.

Fish.info() determines the shell version by invoking a single subprocess with the argument list ['fish', '--version'] (with stdout captured and stderr discarded), rather than running `fish -c 'echo $FISH_VERSION'`.
fix_file.match returns a falsy value when a pattern matches the stderr but the matched 'file' group does not name a path that exists as a file on the filesystem (os.path.isfile is false).
_get_aliases parses alias lines of the form `alias <name>=<value>` (separated by an equals sign, with no space available to split on) into a `name: value` entry.

git_push.match returns True only when command.output contains the literal substring 'git push --set-upstream' (in addition to 'push' appearing in command.script_parts); an output that mentions 'set-upstream' without that full literal phrase (e.g. a successful push whose branch name contains 'set-upstream') does not match.
_get_operations reads the dnf help output from the subprocess stdout and decodes it as UTF-8 before parsing, so the text passed to _parse_operations is a str (not bytes).

When an upstream option ('--set-upstream' or '-u') is present in command.script_parts at an index, get_new_command removes the argument at that index (the option itself) and then attempts to remove the element now occupying that same index; if that second removal fails because the index is out of range, it is silently ignored rather than propagating an IndexError.
WebSocketProtocol declares set_nodelay(x) as an abstract method, so any concrete subclass of WebSocketProtocol that does not implement set_nodelay cannot be instantiated (TypeError).

HTTP1Connection._can_keep_alive does not raise AttributeError when start_line is a response start line (i.e. an object without a `method` attribute), such as httputil.parse_response_start_line('HTTP/1.0 200 OK'); the call completes and returns a boolean instead of raising.

For a client-mode HTTP/1.1 request whose method is POST, PUT, or PATCH, which has no Content-Length header and whose Transfer-Encoding header is present with the exact value "chunked", HTTP1Connection.write_headers enables chunked output encoding (i.e. the body written is chunk-framed and finish() emits the terminating zero-length chunk) instead of treating the explicitly supplied Transfer-Encoding as an externally managed encoding.

AsyncHTTPClient.close() does not raise RuntimeError when the per-IOLoop instance-cache slot for self.io_loop holds the value None (e.g. when the entry was cleared by a weakref before a destructor-driven close runs); the call returns normally and leaves the client marked closed.

The unsatisfiability (416) determination in StaticFileHandler.get is made using the start offset after negative-start resolution and, in addition to the existing triggers (start not None and start >= size, or end == 0), also treats a range as unsatisfiable when end is not None and start >= end; in every such case the response is status 416 with Content-Type text/plain and Content-Range 'bytes */<size>'.

IOLoop._ioloop_for_asyncio is a plain dict (not a WeakKeyDictionary) mapping asyncio event loop objects to IOLoop instances, so its entries persist until explicitly removed rather than expiring on garbage collection of the key.

If the function submitted to IOLoop.run_in_executor raises, the returned Tornado future is completed with that exception (the exception is propagated through the returned future rather than only being stored on the underlying concurrent future).

When a WebSocket client request is missing or has invalid required headers (Host, Sec-Websocket-Key, Sec-Websocket-Version), WebSocketProtocol13.accept_connection responds with HTTP status code 400 instead of aborting the connection.
tenumerate(iterable, start=N) returns an iterator whose yielded index values begin at N (matching builtin enumerate(iterable, start=N)) rather than always beginning at 0.
tqdm defines a Python-2 compatible `__nonzero__` method whose result is identical to `__bool__` (delegates to __bool__), so boolean coercion works the same on Python 2 and Python 3.

tqdm.format_meter does not raise an exception when called with a falsy (None or 0) total together with a custom numeric unit_scale (unit_scale not in (True, 1)); it returns the stats-only formatted string instead.

An instance constructed with disable=True and no explicit `total` stores `total` as its iterable's length when that is obtainable; e.g. tqdm([0], disable=True).total == 1, tqdm([], disable=True).total == 0, so bool() is True for a non-empty iterable and False for an empty one. When the length cannot be obtained (len(iterable) raises TypeError or AttributeError), the stored total is None.

tqdm.__len__ falls back to the instance's `total` attribute when the iterable has neither a `shape` attribute nor a `__len__` method, and returns `None` (rather than raising AttributeError) for instances where `total` was never set, such as a bar constructed with `disable=True` or one that raised TqdmKeyError for unknown kwargs.

format_sizeof promotes a value to the next SI unit postfix before its fixed-point rendering could display four (or more) digits in the current unit: e.g. format_sizeof(999.99) yields '1.00K' (not '1000'), and format_sizeof(999.99, suffix='B') yields '1.00KB'.

For a bare unary filter part `key` (no comparison operator) whose value in the dict is a boolean, _match_one returns True only when the value is True and returns False when the value is False — i.e. a boolean field with value False no longer passes the bare form even though it is not None.
js_to_json matches a single-quoted string that contains a backslash-escaped double quote (\") as one complete string literal, rather than ending the match at that quote.

YoutubeIE._extract_chapters_from_json returns a falsy value (None) without raising when no JSON chapter data can be obtained from the webpage: the webpage is missing/empty, the RELATED_PLAYER_ARGS JSON is absent or unparseable, the parsed player object is not a dict, the watch_next_response entry is absent or not a string, the parsed watch_next_response is not a dict, or the nested chapter list is absent/empty.

The number of returned formats includes a distinct entry for every processed video/audio Representation, so duplicate representation ids produce duplicate (same format_id) entries rather than being collapsed into a single entry.
When path is a bytes object that fails to decode as UTF-8, urljoin propagates the decoding error instead of returning None.

Within a quoted operand, the enclosing quote character may be escaped with a backslash (e.g. 'description = "a\"b"'), and the escaped sequence is unescaped in the comparison value (\" becomes " and \' becomes ').

When the comparison value is treated as a string (either because the filter part explicitly gave a string value, or because the field's actual value is a string and the filter value is numeric), only the '=' and '!=' operators are allowed; any other comparison operator (<, <=, >, >=) raises ValueError('Operator %s does not support string values!' % op).

js_to_json converts the string content of a JavaScript string literal back to numeric form only when that content is entirely a hex or octal numeral (with optional trailing whitespace/colon); otherwise the literal is preserved/returned as a quoted string rather than being truncated to a numeric prefix (e.g. input content '07777abc' stays the string "07777abc" instead of becoming 4095).

js_to_json recognizes a hexadecimal (0x/0X...) or octal (0 followed by octal digits) numeric literal only when it starts at a word boundary; when the leading '0' is immediately preceded by a word character (letter, digit, or underscore) the sequence is not treated as a number literal and is left unconverted (e.g. js_to_json('10xff') leaves '10xff' rather than producing '1255'), while a literal that does start at a word boundary is still converted to its decimal form as before (e.g. '{0xff:0xff}' still maps to {'255': 255}, and '{077:077}' still maps to {'63': 63}).

parse_dfxp_time_expr accepts a clock-form timestamp whose seconds component uses a colon as the fractional separator (e.g. 'HH:MM:SS:sss'), returning the corresponding number of seconds as a float; previously such input produced None.

_htmlentity_transform returns the literal string '&<entity>;' when the entity matches the numeric-reference form (#<digits> or #x<hexdigits>) but its codepoint is not a valid character (e.g. '&#2013266066;' yields '&#2013266066;'), instead of letting the chr() conversion's ValueError propagate (so unescapeHTML does not raise on such input).

When the format-selector function produced by build_format_selector for a direct (single) format token is applied to an empty collection of formats, it yields no formats instead of raising an error (e.g. for 'best'/'worst' it no longer indexes into an empty list).

parse_duration accepts a string consisting solely of a number followed by a minutes unit ('min', 'mins', 'minute', 'minutes', case-insensitive) and returns that number of minutes converted to seconds (value * 60, e.g. '10 mins' -> 600.0), rather than returning None.

youtube_dl.utils.strip_jsonp extracts the JSON payload from a JSONP-wrapped string by removing the leading callback wrapper and returns only the captured argument text, including when the JSONP code is followed by a trailing '//' line comment: e.g. for input like 'parseMetadata({...});\n// trailing comment' the returned string is the '{...}' payload with neither the wrapper, the trailing ';' nor the trailing '//' comment.
ArteTVPlus7IE._extract_from_json_url sets the resulting info_dict 'upload_date' from the JSON field 'shootingDate' when that field is present and non-empty, rather than from the 'VDA' field.

youtube_dl.utils exposes a function urlencode_postdata that URL-encodes its arguments (forwarding *args/**kargs to compat_urllib_parse.urlencode) and returns the result encoded as an ASCII bytes object rather than a str.
limit_length(s, length) returns None when s is None (it does not raise a TypeError).

JSInterpreter.interpret_expression accepts a JS function-call expression with an empty argument list, e.g. 'x()', as a valid supported expression rather than falling through to 'Unsupported JS expression'.
youtube_dl.utils exposes a module-level callable named struct_pack whose call signature is struct_pack(spec, *args) and which behaves like the standard struct.pack for all valid inputs.
youtube_dl.utils exposes a function named fix_xml_ampersands(xml_str) that takes an XML string and returns a string.

unified_timestamp, when the input date string fails every date_formats() strptime pattern and is instead parsed by email.utils.parsedate_tz, now includes a 12-hour (43200-second) positive offset in the returned UNIX timestamp whenever the original input contains 'PM' (case-insensitive), so e.g. unified_timestamp('May 16, 2016 11:15 PM') returns the PM-corrected timestamp rather than the AM one.
parse_dfxp_time_expr returns None (not 0.0) when time_expr is falsy (empty string, None, or 0).

YoutubeDL.build_format_selector accepts a format specification that combines a '/' choice with a top-level ',' list at the same nesting level (e.g. 'bestvideo/best,worst') and returns a usable format-selector function without raising an error.

In a format specification, the right-hand operand of the '+' (merge) operator terminates at an unparenthesized '/' or ',' instead of absorbing it, so '/' and ',' bind looser than '+': e.g. 'bestvideo+bestaudio/best' selects the pick-first between the merged 'bestvideo+bestaudio' pair and 'best', rather than merging bestvideo with the choice (bestaudio/best).

When reading a table from a filename or file-like input with memmap=True, invalid-value masking (NaNs in float/complex columns and empty strings in character columns) is unconditionally disabled: mask_invalid is set to False regardless of the caller-supplied value of the mask_invalid argument.

Constructing a Time with format='byear' from a value that is a genuine quantity (exposes a 'to' method and a non-None 'unit') still raises ValueError with the message 'Cannot use Quantities for \'byear\' format...', but a value that happens to expose 'to' and 'unit' attributes whose unit is None is no longer rejected and is instead handled as an ordinary numeric Besselian-year input.

When called with as_image_hdu=True, fits_ccddata_writer (reached via CCDData.write) writes the CCDData data into an ImageHDU extension while prepending an effectively data-free PrimaryHDU as element 0 of the written FITS file, so the file's first HDU is a PrimaryHDU and the data lives in the following ImageHDU; when as_image_hdu is False or omitted, the file is written as before with the data in the PrimaryHDU.

Cosmology read/write I/O offers 'ascii.html' as a registered format: once astropy.cosmology.io is imported (which now imports io.html), Cosmology.read and Cosmology.write accept format='ascii.html' and Cosmology.read with no format can auto-identify an ascii.html file by its '.html' filename suffix.

An Angle whose unit is specified as hours (u.hour or an hour unit that compares equal to u.hour) is normalized to hourangle, so that to_string() of such an angle (or when u.hour is passed as the to_string unit) yields hourangle/hms sexagesimal rather than being treated as a non-degree, non-hour-angle angular unit.

Indexing a Quantity whose unit is a StructuredUnit with a string field key (returning the sub-quantity corresponding to that field) produces a result that does not inherit the source quantity's per-instance `info`; only the field's unit is assigned to the new view.

When a WCS is constructed from a header whose (default-key) CTYPE codes end in '-TAN' on exactly two axes and at least one of those '-TAN' axes carries a PV keyword with subscript j >= 5, those CTYPE codes are rewritten to end in '-TPV' in the resulting core WCS (so the WCS uses the TPV projection) and the SIP distortion is not loaded (the resulting WCS.sip is None), while a FITSFixedWarning with message 'Removed redundant SIP distortion parameters because SCAMP' PV distortions are also present' is emitted.

Latex's to_string no longer unconditionally appends r'\,' immediately after the formatted exponential scale of a non-unity-scale CompositeUnit; the r'\,' separator is emitted only when the composite actually has basis units following the scale (so a scaled CompositeUnit with no bases produces no dangling thin-space separator).
Calling/set_enabled_constants with any modname other than the supported 'astropyconst13' raises ValueError with a message naming the unsupported modname, before any constant values are changed.

Constructing a TimeDelta whose val is a datetime.timedelta object (or iterable thereof) without an explicit `format` now succeeds, auto-selecting the 'datetime' format, rather than raising an error about only Quantities being usable.

biweight_midvariance of a constant (flattened, axis=None) input array, for which the median absolute deviation is 0, returns 0.0 instead of a NaN/inf result arising from division by zero (so biweight_scale of constant data returns 0.0).

On SQLite, evaluating LPAD, REPEAT, or RPAD with any NULL argument (e.g. a NULL text or NULL length arising from a NULL column) returns NULL rather than raising a user-defined-function error, so text functions using those build NULL results for NULL inputs.

An app-label argument that refers to an app which is installed in INSTALLED_APPS but has no migrations is no longer treated as an error: validation only rejects labels that fail apps.get_app_config (non-installed), so such an installed-but-unmigrated app no longer causes the process to raise an error or exit non-zero for that reason.

For a non-add object change with non-empty changed form data, the returned change_message's top-level {'changed': {'fields': [...]}} entry must list each changed form field by its verbose label rather than its raw attribute name — each label being the corresponding form field's .label, with the raw field name used when that field has no (empty) .label or is not present as a field on the form.

Preparing a value containing an aggregate expression for an INSERT raises FieldError whose message is 'Aggregate functions are not allowed in this query (fieldname=value).' — i.e. it ends with an interpolation of the target field's name and the resolved expression, rather than the bare 'Aggregate functions are not allowed in this query'.

A new backend capability flag features.supports_frame_range_fixed_distance is introduced: it defaults to False on the base BaseDatabaseFeatures (so most backends report False), while the Oracle backend (DatabaseFeatures.supports_frame_range_fixed_distance) is declared True, advertising that Oracle supports RANGE window frames at a fixed non-None distance.

When USE_TZ is enabled and the requested timezone name differs from the connection timezone and encodes a fixed offset via an inline '+' or '-' sign (a datetime.timezone-style name), the CONVERT_TZ target argument is reduced to just the signed-offset tail starting at that sign (e.g. 'UTC+05:00' -> '+05:00', sign kept as written), rather than passing the full name, so that MySQL interprets the fixed Unicode offset; datetimes converted to a fixed-offset timezone thereby reflect that nominal offset. Names lacking such an inline sign are used unchanged.

For a Media produced by summing other Media objects (m1 + m2 + ... + mn, in any nesting/grouping of the + operations), each CSS output medium's path list is built by merging that medium's paths across the css dictionaries of the base operands in their source addition order — a css medium appearing in any operand is present in the result, later-operand paths that duplicate earlier ones are not re-added, empty css members are inert, and parenthesization of the sum does not change any medium's resulting path list.

The datetime appended to applied `--list` lines is the applied migration record's `applied` timestamp converted via strftime with the exact format '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', yielding a wall-clock string like '2021-01-01 12:00:00'.

ModelChoiceField.to_python accepts a value that is already an instance of the queryset's model by extracting the value's to_field_name attribute (defaulting to the model's pk) and using that extracted value for the queryset lookup; this resolves to the cached DB object rather than raising an invalid_choice ValidationError as was the case when the model instance itself was passed as the lookup parameter.
When the UserCreationForm's model USERNAME_FIELD is present in self.fields, that field's widget renders with the attribute autocomplete="username" (in addition to its retained autofocus="").

Running the system checks on a BinaryField that has an explicit default which is a str (e.g. BinaryField(default='') or any other str default) returns a checks.Error with id 'fields.E170' and obj set to that field.

When register() is called on a model that is already in the registry and whose existing registration entry's admin object string representation ends with '.ModelAdmin' (i.e. the model was registered with a plain default ModelAdmin), it raises AlreadyRegistered whose message is exactly "The model <ModelName> is already registered in app '<s>'. " where <s> is that string representation with the trailing '.ModelAdmin' removed (e.g. the plain ModelAdmin's module path such as django.contrib.admin.options).

For each unresolvable custom error handler, the emitted urls.E008 Error's message exactly equals "The custom handler{status_code} view '{path}' could not be imported.", where status_code is the numeric handler code (400/403/404/500) and path is the string value stored in the urlconf module's handler{status_code} attribute at the time of the failure.

If accessing the URLconf module (get_resolver().urlconf_module) at reloader startup raises any Exception, the error is swallowed and reloader startup continues: the autoreload_started signal is still sent and the reloader's poll loop still runs instead of the exception propagating.

When a relation column is the table's primary key (a PK-FK column), inspectdb generates the field definition as a OneToOneField rather than a ForeignKey, preserving the explicit `primary_key=True` parameter and still including `models.DO_NOTHING` (e.g. `models.OneToOneField(InspectdbPeople, models.DO_NOTHING, primary_key=True)`).

In page_not_found, when the default 404.html template is unavailable (TemplateDoesNotExist for the default template name), the returned HttpResponseNotFound body is a complete HTML5 document that starts with '' and ends with '', with a containing "Not Found" and a containing "

Not Found

" followed by a

whose text is 'The requested resource was not found on this server.'

For a command that declares subcommands via parser.add_subparsers(), when a required argument declared on the selected subcommand's parser (rather than on the top-level parser) is supplied through call_command's **options, call_command forwards that required argument into its argument-parsing simulation and the command executes successfully — it does not raise (e.g. a ValueError from reading option strings, or an argparse error/CommandError about a missing required argument) during option reconstruction.

When ServerHandler.cleanup_headers() runs for a response and the server that served it is not a socketserver.ThreadingMixIn instance (i.e. a non-threaded HTTP server), the 'Connection' header is set to 'close' even if the response does include a 'Content-Length' header, so the request handler's connection is marked for closing (close_connection becomes True) and a subsequent request is not kept alive on that connection.

AutoField.get_prep_value, when the value passed after super().get_prep_value is not None and not an OuterRef and cannot be converted by int(value), raises an exception of the same class as the one int(value) raised (TypeError or ValueError), whose message is "Field '%s' expected a number but got %r." % (self.name, value), with the original conversion error chained via 'from e'.

When settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS is non-empty, the Warning emitted for a duplicate db_table carries hint text "You have configured settings.DATABASE_ROUTERS. Verify that {comma-space-joined colliding model labels} are correctly routed to separate databases.", whereas when routers are not configured the report carries no hint.

When django.utils.http.urlencode is called with queries whose direct mapping value for a key is None (the outer loop guard, regardless of doseq), the TypeError raised has message "Cannot encode None for key '<key>' in a query string. Did you mean to pass an empty string or omit the value?", where '<key>' is replaced with the offending key.

The security.W019 deploy-check warning message text is changed: when XFrameOptionsMiddleware is present in MIDDLEWARE and X_FRAME_OPTIONS is not 'DENY', the reported warning now reads "You have 'django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware' in your MIDDLEWARE, but X_FRAME_OPTIONS is not set to 'DENY'. Unless there is a good reason for your site to serve other parts of itself in a frame, you should change it to 'DENY'." — it no longer contains the sentence "The default is 'SAMEORIGIN', but".

make_template_fragment_key no longer URL-encodes vary_on values before hashing: characters that urllib.parse.quote would percent-encode (such as ':', '/', '%', whitespace, or non-ASCII characters) now contribute to the fragment-key MD5 digest in their raw string form, so the returned 'template.cache.<fragment>.<digest>' differs from the old percent-encoded-digest for such inputs.

When the rhs value supplied to an isnull lookup is not a bool instance (True or False), compiling that lookup (IsNull.as_sql) emits a RemovedInDjango40Warning carrying the message 'Using a non-boolean value for an isnull lookup is deprecated, use True or False instead.'; a bool rhs (True or False) does not emit any such warning.

django.views.debug.technical_500_response now selects its response body format by Accept-header content negotiation: if request.accepts('text/html') it returns an HTML traceback with content_type='text/html' and status_code; otherwise it returns a plain-text traceback with content_type='text/plain; charset=utf-8'. The choice no longer depends on the X-Requested-With (is_ajax) header.
ManifestFilesMixin's constructor accepts a keyword argument manifest_storage and stores it on the instance as the manifest_storage attribute.

Query.set_group_by() treats an annotation's get_group_by_cols method as accepting the alias argument only if that method's signature declares a parameter named 'alias'. If it does declare such a parameter, get_group_by_cols is called as get_group_by_cols(alias=<annotation alias>); if it does not (including legacy methods that would absorb alias only via **kwargs), a RemovedInDjango40Warning whose text is '`alias=None` must be added to the signature of <module>.<qualname>.get_group_by_cols().' (module and qualname taken from the annotation's class) is emitted and get_group_by_cols() is called with no arguments. In both cases the returned group-by columns are merged into the query's GROUP BY clause.

When django.forms.models._get_foreign_key is called with no fk_name and the model has more than one ForeignKey to parent_model (i.e. the pathological over-disambiguation case), the ValueError it raises now has the full message: “'<model._meta.label>' has more than one ForeignKey to '<parent_model._meta.label>'. You must specify a 'fk_name' attribute.” — i.e. the message appends the guidance sentence "You must specify a 'fk_name' attribute." to the pre-existing prefix.

Options.total_unique_constraints returns the list of objects in Meta.constraints that are UniqueConstraint instances whose condition attribute is None (i.e., unconditional/total unique constraints); UniqueConstraint instances with a non-None condition (partial constraints) and constraint objects that are not UniqueConstraint instances (e.g. CheckConstraint) are excluded from the returned list.

When resolving a 'pk' ordering lookup (the pk shortcut), if the model's pk is a relation field (e.g. the parent pointer under multi-table inheritance) pointing to a model that declares its own Meta.ordering, SQLCompiler.find_ordering_name treats the lookup as an order-by-the-pk-column clause rather than substituting the referenced model's Meta.ordering in its place.

CommandError instances expose a `returncode` attribute whose value is 1 by default and can be set through a `returncode=` keyword argument to the constructor; this applies to every CommandError (and, via inheritance, to subclasses such as SystemCheckError that do not override __init__).

ModelMultipleChoiceField.__init__() emits a RemovedInDjango40Warning whenever the field's assembled error_messages still contain the deprecated 'list' key (e.g. supplied via the error_messages kwarg), and in that case copies the value of that 'list' override onto the 'invalid_list' key so the override still takes effect.

When make_password raises TypeError for a non-bytes/str, non-None password, the exception message uses the __qualname__ of the passed password's type in the text 'Password must be a string or bytes, got <qualname>.'

DatabaseOperations.sql_flush's signature is changed (in base and every backend) from (style, tables, sequences, allow_cascade) to (style, tables, *, reset_sequences=False, allow_cascade=False): the positional sequences argument is removed and sequence-reset behavior is instead requested via the keyword-only reset_sequences boolean (default False). Passing a sequences argument positionally now raises a TypeError.

When `loader.check_consistent_history(connection)` for a per-connection history check raises `django.db.OperationalError`, the `makemigrations` command no longer lets that exception abort execution; instead it catches it and continues to run to normal completion (conflict detection and onward), so the command does not exit with an error solely because a database connection could not be reached.

When the template engine parses a template containing the built-in {% ifequal %}{% endifequal %} tag (invoking the registered ifequal tag function), it emits a Python deprecation warning of category RemovedInDjango40Warning (a PendingDeprecationWarning subclass) with a message stating that the {% ifequal %} template tag is deprecated in favor of {% if %}.

Every call to django.conf.urls.url(regex, view, kwargs=None, name=None) emits a deprecation warning whose category is RemovedInDjango40Warning (a subclass of PendingDeprecationWarning) and whose message text is 'django.conf.urls.url() is deprecated in favor of django.urls.re_path().'

If a FilteredRelation's relation_name itself fails to resolve to a plain chain of relationship fields (i.e. solving it leaves leftover lookup/transform segments), add_filtered_relation raises ValueError with message 'FilteredRelation\'s relation_name cannot contain lookups (got %r).' identifying the offending relation_name.

When SessionMiddleware.process_response takes the session-deletion branch (SESSION_COOKIE_NAME present in request cookies and session empty), the deletion cookie is now written with samesite=settings.SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE, so the emptied session cookie carries the SameSite attribute from the SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE setting.

In MigrationLoader.load_disk, once an app's migrations module is confirmed to be a regular (non-namespace) package (it has both a __file__ and a __path__), the app's label is added to migrated_apps unconditionally — the previously conditional logic that would instead add it to unmigrated_apps when the package contained no migration submodules and ignore_no_migrations was False is removed, so an app with a real but empty migrations package is now treated as migrated regardless of the number of migration submodules it contains and regardless of the ignore_no_migrations value.

When autodetection changes an already-existing (kept) model whose `order_with_respect_to` option changes and which simultaneously has index/unique/index_together/constraint/db-table changes to emit, the `AlterOrderWithRespectTo` operation for that model is generated (and therefore ordered) before the added-index, altered-unique-together, altered-index-together, added-constraint, and altered-db-table operations belonging to the same autodetection run, so schema referencing the ordering's `_order` column is not added ahead of the ordering operation.

When the state for a model instance is produced by Model.__getstate__, FK/related-value entries already present in the source instance's ModelState.fields_cache are carried over as copied entries into the returned state's copied fields_cache (rather than being dropped or shared by reference), so a shallow copy or unpickled copy of an already-populated instance retains its prior cached related values independently of any later mutations to the original's cache.

When an app module's default_app_config does not equal the auto-detected configuration and automatic detection found no configuration at all (app_config_name is None), the emitted RemovedInDjango41Warning message contains the text "However, Django's automatic detection did not find this configuration." rather than referencing a (None) picked configuration.

When update_fields names a field(s) not in the validated non-primary-key concrete-field set, Model.save raises ValueError whose message enumerates the offending fields as not existing, being m2m, or being non-concrete fields ('The following fields do not exist in this model, are m2m fields, or are non-concrete fields: <comma-separated names>') rather than the prior text that omitted the non-concrete-field clause.

When SessionBase.decode is given session data whose signing.loads decode raises signing.BadSignature AND whose legacy decode path (_legacy_decode) also raises an exception, decode does NOT propagate an exception: it logs a warning 'Session data corrupted' to the 'django.security.SuspiciousSession' logger and returns an empty dict {}.

TemplateView.get passes the keyword arguments it receives from dispatch (URLconf-captured URL kwargs) directly into the template context, so each URL keyword argument name maps in the rendered context to its ordinary raw value, no longer wrapped in a lazy/deferred object.

A combined arithmetic expression (CombinedExpression using ADD, SUB, MUL or DIV) whose two source sub-expressions have output fields that are integer-kind fields — i.e. any pair that are each IntegerField or an IntegerField subclass such as AutoField, SmallAutoField or BigAutoField (distinct classes, e.g. a plain IntegerField from Value(3) combined with an AutoField column) — resolves to an IntegerField output instead of raising a 'mixed output-field types' FieldError.

When rendering a blocktranslate/blocktrans tag that carries a plural count (i.e. a `count` option that provides both a counter variable and counter expression), if the value that the counter expression resolves to in the render context is not one of the numeric types Decimal, float, or int (e.g. it is a str, list, None, or other non-numeric type), render() raises a TemplateSyntaxError rather than proceeding to plural-form selection and '%'-formatting. The raised error's message is "%r argument to %r tag must be a number." where the first %r is the counter variable name and the second is the tag name (blocktranslate/blocktrans).

call_command, when a required option or a member of a required mutually exclusive group is supplied via **options and that option's argparse action is one that stores a constant without taking an argument (store_true/store_false/store_const via _StoreConstAction, count via _CountAction, or append_const via _AppendConstAction), must pass it into the simulated parser as the bare option flag (e.g. '--flag') rather than '--flag=<value>', so the command executes instead of failing with an argparse parsing error/CommandError over an invalid '--flag=<value>' token.

When deletion via Collector.collect is blocked by protected foreign keys and it aggregates references into a ProtectedError, the raised exception's `protected_objects` attribute (and the second positional element of its `args` tuple, which is what its repr renders) is a materialized `set` of the referencing objects — never a lazy iterator such as an `itertools.chain` — so the attribute is directly inspectable/iterable and each distinct referencing object appears once.

In BaseFormSet.management_form, when the formset is bound and the submitted ManagementForm is invalid, the raised ValidationError (code 'missing_management_form') carries a message that begins with 'ManagementForm data is missing or has been tampered with' followed by a suffix 'Missing fields: <names>', where <names> is the comma-and-space joined list of form.add_prefix(field_name) applied to each field that appears in form.errors.

Calling QuerySet.bulk_create() with an object whose concrete ForeignKey/OneToOne relation is cached (assigned) to an object that has no pk (obj.pk is None) raises a ValueError with message "bulk_create() prohibited to prevent data loss due to unsaved related object '<field name>'." instead of inserting the row.

When makemessages processes files whose translations cannot be assigned to a locale path (locale_dir is NO_LOCALE_DIR) but messages were produced, the raised CommandError message is: "Unable to find a locale path to store translations for file <normpath-of-first-build-file>. Make sure the 'locale' directory exist in an app or LOCALE_PATHS setting is set." (precisely, the message equals the concatenation given, i.e. there is a file path after 'file ' and the sentence is followed by the hint text).

When a positional (non-keyword) argument passed to call_command (an element of the *args sequence) is a list or tuple, each element of that collection is stringified with str() and treated as a separate token in the simulated argument parse, so that a collection supplied for an nargs-style positional resolves to its individual parsed values rather than one token holding the whole collection's str() representation.

URLPattern.check() reports a system-check Error with id 'urls.E009' when the pattern's callback is a class (not an instance) that subclasses django.views.View, whose message describes the pattern and advises passing {ViewName}.as_view() instead of the class itself.

The durability nesting check of Atomic is subject to the class-level private flag Atomic._ensure_durability (True by default) such that when a subclass (or instance class) sets _ensure_durability to False, entering a durable=True atomic block nested inside another atomic block no longer raises RuntimeError.

ModelAdmin now defines the public method get_formset_kwargs(self, request, obj, inline, prefix), exposing a subclass-overridable point for computing the keyword arguments with which each inline formset is instantiated.

Constructing django.core.cache.backends.memcached.MemcachedCache (calling MemcachedCache(server, params)) emits a RemovedInDjango41Warning whose message states that MemcachedCache is deprecated in favor of PyMemcacheCache and PyLibMCCache.

When dumpdata runs with --output on a path whose extension is '.zip' (always) or '.bz2'/'.lzma'/'.xz' while the corresponding compression module (bz2, lzma, lzma) is not importable, the fixture is instead written as plain text into a file at the output path with that extension stripped, and a RuntimeWarning is issued whose text names the unsupported extension (e.g. "Unsupported file extension (.zip)") and the actual file the fixture was saved to (the basename of that stripped path).
In get_connection_params, when settings NAME is None, the returned connection params set database to 'postgres' and do not forward any 'service' OPTIONS entry to psycopg2.

ExceptionReporter.html_template_path and text_template_path yield the paths of the builtin technical_500.html and technical_500.txt templates (resolved lazily via builtin_template_path) rather than via a module-level constant; technical_404_response and default_urlconf read technical_404.html and default_urlconf.html from the same lazily-derived builtin template directory.

On the SQLite backend, an exact-equality filter on a JSON member against one of the JSON literals true, false, or null (field__key=True / field__key=False / field__key=None) selects exactly the rows whose stored JSON value at that key equals that JSON literal, and does not additionally match rows storing a different JSON literal or an integer of equal SQL value, or rows lacking that key.

django.db.models.fields.related.RelatedField.deconstruct() emits a `related_query_name` entry in its returned kwargs equal to the related_query_name value originally supplied to the field's constructor (snapshotted at construction in self._related_query_name), independent of any later change to remote_field.related_query_name, and omits the key when none was originally supplied.

Field.check() performs a new system check (_check_db_comment) that, for a field with a non-empty db_comment referring to a database whose connection does not advertise supports_comments (and whose model does not require the 'supports_comments' DB feature), returns checks.Warning id 'fields.W163' stating the DB does not support comments on columns (db_comment).

ManyToManyField.check() (via the _check_ignored_options machinery, wired through ManyToManyField.check and model-level check) returns a django.core.checks.Warning with id 'fields.W345', message 'related_name has no effect on ManyToManyField with a symmetrical relationship, e.g. to "self".', and obj set to the field, whenever the field's remote_field.symmetrical is truthy and a truthy related_name was explicitly supplied to the constructor (self._related_name). Conversely, no such W345 warning is emitted when either no related_name was explicitly supplied or the relationship is not symmetrical.

Every concrete cache-operation entry point across the db, dummy, filebased, locmem, and memcached backends (add/get/set/touch/delete/delete_many/has_key/incr/get_many/set_many and DatabaseCache.get_many key mapping) continues to produce a made key and subject that made key to the backend's key-validity check before performing the operation — the same observable warning/error behavior on invalid keys, now routed through make_and_validate_key.

When floatformat is given a string argument ending in the letter 'u' without a preceding 'g' (e.g. '2u', '-3u', 'u'), the formatted result is unlocalized: it uses the default '.' decimal separator and non-locale thousand separator rather than the active locale's separators. E.g. with the pl locale active, 66666.6666|floatformat:"2u" yields "66666.67". (Previously such an argument failed arg parsing and returned the repr of the input.)

When RelatedField._check_clashes() emits the 'fields.E302' Error (a reverse accessor name installed on the related model clashes with an existing field name on that related model, and the relation is not hidden), the Error message text exactly matches `Reverse accessor '{<related-model object_name>}.{<the accessor name>}' for '{<app_label.Model.field the defining field>}' clashes with field name '{<app_label.Target.field the clashing field>}'.` — i.e. the message begins by naming the actual reverse accessor being installed, qualified by the related model's object name.

While generating an AddField operation for an added field, if the (default-adjusted) field being added is unique, has a default that is not models.NOT_PROVIDED, and has a callable default, MigrationAutodetector calls questioner.ask_unique_callable_default_addition(field_name, model_name) for that field; when any of those three conditions is false the hook is not invoked for that field.

In interactive superuser creation, when a REQUIRED_FIELDS option is supplied a non-None value via the command line (rather than being prompted), that value is validated by passing it through field.clean(value, None); if field.clean raises a ValidationError, the command terminates with a CommandError whose message is the ValidationError messages joined by '; ', rather than silently using the raw unvalidated value for the user.

prepare_lookup_value' accepts an optional third argument `separator` (defaulting to `','`); when the lookup key ends with `__in`, it splits the value string into a list on that separator instead of a hard-coded comma (e.g. prepare_lookup_value('x__in', 'a;b', ';') returns ['a','b']), so callers not supplying a separator still get the previous comma-splitting behavior and the __isnull handling is unchanged.

The squashmigrations management command refuses to run when the on-disk destination migration file it would write already exists: instead of creating/overwriting any file at that path, it fails the command by raising CommandError whose message contains the phrase 'already exists' and the new migration name.
MultiWidget.id_for_label(id_) returns the empty string '' for every argument, so that a field-level <label> associated with a MultiWidget never points (via for=) to its first subwidget's HTML id.

Calling path() or re_path() with a kwargs argument that is not None and not a dict raises a TypeError whose message indicates the kwargs argument must be a dict and names the actual type passed (e.g. '...but got str.') instead of proceeding to build the pattern/resolver.
The migrate management command accepts a --prune command-line option (stored as the 'prune' option).

remove_non_capturing_groups(pattern) returns the input URL-regex pattern with each top-level non-capturing group (?:...) removed entirely — its '(?:' opening marker, its balanced matching ')', and all text between them are dropped, while all other text outside such groups is preserved in place — and this holds regardless of where the non-capturing group is located in the pattern (at the start, interior, or end) and regardless of whether its content itself contains further nested groups (which are removed along with the enclosing group). E.g. '^(?:\w+)a' -> '^a'; '^a(?:\w+)/b(?:\w+)' -> '^a/b'; '^(?:\w+(?:\w+))a' -> '^a'; '(?P<a>\w+)/b/(?:\w+)c(?:\w+)' -> '(?P<a>\w+)/b/c'; a pattern with no non-capturing group is returned unchanged.

QuerySet.iterator() called on a QuerySet that currently has prefetch_related() lookups set, with chunk_size omitted (None, the new default), emits a DeprecationWarning whose message starts 'Using QuerySet.iterator() after prefetch_related() without specifying chunk_size is deprecated.', and does not raise an exception.

When BaseHandler.adapt_method_mode adapts a synchronous method for an async mode (is_async=True and method_is_async=False) with debug=True, it emits a DEBUG record on the 'django.request' logger whose formatted message is 'Synchronous handler adapted for {name}.'.

When HttpResponseBase.set_cookie is called with an 'expires' argument that is a datetime.datetime object (a naive datetime interpreted as UTC, or an aware datetime in any time zone) together with a non-None 'max_age' argument, it raises ValueError with message "'expires' and 'max_age' can't be used together." rather than silently computing max_age from expires and discarding the caller-supplied max_age.

When the autodetector generates an AddField for a field on an app/model and the same-change computation also removes a field of that identical name from that model (so the field name must be dropped then re-created, e.g. a ForeignKey/concrete field being replaced by a plain ManyToManyField), the resulting set of migration operations orders the re-adding AddField strictly after the matching RemoveField of that field name — never before it — so a single combined migration can apply both without relying on incidental list order.

When BaseDatabaseWrapper.on_commit is invoked with robust=True while the connection is in autocommit with no atomic block in progress (so func runs immediately), an exception raised by func is caught and logged instead of being propagated out of the on_commit call, which returns normally; when robust=False (the default), an exception from func propagates out of that immediate on_commit call unchanged.

URLField.to_python (and therefore URLField.clean) prepends the field's configured scheme (self.assume_scheme) rather than a hard-coded 'http' to scheme-less URL inputs, so the scheme prepended to a scheme-less value such as 'example.com' is whatever scheme the field was constructed with.

When a StepValueValidator is constructed with a non-None offset and the value fails the step check, the raised ValidationError conveys code "step_size" with the offset-aware message text ("starting from %(offset)s, e.g. %(offset)s, %(valid_value1)s, %(valid_value2)s, and so on.") and params limit_value, offset, valid_value1 (= offset + limit_value), and valid_value2 (= offset + 2*limit_value).

In the ModelAdmin system checks, a list_display item whose value (obtained via obj.model._meta.get_field(item) or via the fallback getattr(obj.model, item)) is a reverse one-to-many relation (a reverse foreign key, i.e. the field's .rel exists and field.rel.field.many_to_one is true) is rejected with a checks.Error carrying id 'admin.E109' whose message reads "The value of '<label>' must not be a many-to-many field or a reverse foreign key.".

Figure(...) construction raises ValueError (with a message stating the size must be positive finite) when the figsize argument has any dimension that is non-finite or not strictly positive (i.e. zero or negative), so a figure whose width or height is 0 or negative is never successfully constructed.

A legend created with a string loc whose first space-separated token is 'outside' (e.g. 'outside upper left', 'outside upper center', 'outside upper right', 'outside lower center', 'outside lower right', 'outside lower left', 'outside right upper', 'outside right lower', 'outside left upper', 'outside left lower') is accepted: the 'outside' token is consumed and the remainder is mapped onto an otherwise valid standard loc value, so construction succeeds rather than failing as an unrecognized loc. The token order matters ('outside right upper' maps to a different resolved location than 'outside upper right').

Calling selector.set_handle_props(**handle_props) applies the given properties to each of the selector's handle/vertex artists (e.g. RectangleSelector corner/edge/center markers, SpanSelector edge handles, PolygonSelector vertex handles), so their rendered appearance is updated immediately; the props are also recorded in _handle_props for future handles.

copy.copy of a TaggedValue returns a new TaggedValue holding the same value and unit as the original (shallow copy, sharing the underlying value object), rather than falling back to deep/reduce-based copying.

In PS/EPS output, when a clip-path that has not been seen before is drawn, RendererPS defines a bound PostScript procedure whose name is 'c' followed by the clip path's zero-based sequence number formatted in decimal (so the clip procedures defined/used in the emitted .ps/.eps file are c0, c1, ..., c10, ... rather than c0,c1,...,ca,cb,... for counts >= 10), and that decimal name (not a hexadecimal rendering) is the value cached in _clip_paths and re-referenced whenever the same clip path recurs.

ContourSet.find_nearest_contour(x, y, indices=None, pixel=True) raises ValueError (carrying the message "Method does not support filled contours.") when invoked on a filled ContourSet (self.filled is True), regardless of the value of the indices argument.

When tripcolor is called with neither a positional C argument nor a 'facecolors' keyword (facecolors is None and no positional arg remains after the triangulation spec is consumed), it raises a TypeError (not ValueError) whose message is "tripcolor() missing 1 required positional argument: 'C'; or 1 required keyword-only argument: 'facecolors'".

After pyplot.switch_backend() completes a switch to a concrete (named, non-auto-sentinel) backend, the current shell's REPL/pylab display hook is (re)installed: in an interactive matplotlib session -- including an IPython '--pylab' session where install_repl_displayhook registers pyplot._draw_all_if_interactive as the IPython post_execute handler -- figures are automatically re-drawn at the end of subsequent input commands (interactive auto-redraw is active). This holds whether the backend load is the session's first lazy load through _get_backend_mod or a later explicit backend switch reached through any other entry point; previously the hook was installed only inside _get_backend_mod's `if _backend_mod is None` first-lazy-load branch, so a backend switch performed once a backend was already loaded (e.g. via an explicit switch_backend / matplotlib.use call) left the auto-redraw display hook unregistered.

matplotlib.style.use (and the style.context context manager, which delegates to use) accepts, as a style specification, a string of the dotted form "package.style_name" where "package" is an importable Python package; the rcParams defined in the file located inside that package at <package>/style_name.mplstyle are read and applied (only the parameters actually listed in that file). Dotted names spanning subpackages (e.g. "dotted.package.name" resolving within dotted/package/) are likewise supported.

Calling Axis.set_ticks with labels=None (labels not provided) while passing additional keyword arguments raises ValueError with the message 'labels argument cannot be None when kwargs are passed', rather than silently ignoring those kwargs.

A constructed Legend instance exposes a public instance attribute `legend_handles` whose value is the list of Artist objects actually added as legend-handle entries (one per retained legend entry, in the same order and aligned with `legend.texts`); the list is reassigned at the end of `_init_legend_box` to the finalized `handle_list`, and it is precisely the list that `get_lines`, `get_patches`, and the labelcolor color-getter loop read from.

In the mesh-data setup shared by pcolor/pcolormesh (Axes._pcolorargs), the number of rows and columns of the mesh is derived from the first two dimensions of C only, so C with more than two dimensions (notably 3D RGB(A) image data of shape (M,N,3) or (M,N,4)) is accepted rather than raising an unpacking error; the mesh is laid out on an M×N grid of the leading dims.

imsave raises a ValueError (with a message indicating the format does not support metadata) instead of silently ignoring *metadata* when saving to any raster format handled by Pillow other than 'png' (e.g. jpeg, tiff, webp); metadata continues to be honoured for 'png' and for the vector formats 'pdf'/'ps'/'eps'/'svg', and a None metadata still passes through unchanged.

Calling grab_frame(savefig_kwargs=...) where savefig_kwargs contains the key 'dpi', 'bbox_inches', or 'format' raises a TypeError (rejected before the frame is saved), because those arguments are controlled by the MovieWriter.

Calling Axis.set_ticks(ticks) (with labels=None and minor not given) while passing one or more extra keyword-only styling/Text arguments (i.e. kwargs is non-empty) raises a ValueError whose message states 'Incorrect use of keyword argument' followed by the repr of the first such keyword argument passed, and goes on to say that keyword arguments other than 'minor' modify the text labels and can only be used if 'labels' are passed as well.

seaborn.external.version.Version parses a PEP-440 version string (with optional epoch, pre/post/dev/local segments); constructing it from an invalid version string raises InvalidVersion (a ValueError subclass), and its ordering comparisons follow PEP 440 normalization so that e.g. '3.0' and '3.0.0' compare equal and pre/post/dev/local orderings are respected.

For a vector that is not entirely missing, variable_type determines the reported type from only the present (non-null) entries: it first returns 'numeric' only when every entry is missing; otherwise it removes all missing entries and then applies boolean detection and numeric/datetime/categorical inference to the remaining values. Concretely, an object/extension column that (ignoring nulls) is made up solely of numeric values is reported as 'numeric' rather than categorical, and one made up solely of datetime values as 'datetime', regardless of the presence/position of missing entries.

HTTPAdapter.send catches a urllib3 ClosedPoolError raised by the connection operation and re-raises it as a requests.exceptions.ConnectionError (constructed from the original exception with request=request), rather than letting the raw urllib3 exception escape to the caller.

DataArray and Dataset (both subclassing common.DataWithCoords) each expose a `weighted(weights)` method that returns a weighted-operations accessor object constructed from the object under reduction and the provided weights (`DataArrayWeighted` for DataArray, `DatasetWeighted` for Dataset).
When max_gap is provided and is not a scalar (e.g. any array-like or list), interpolate_na raises ValueError with message 'max_gap must be a scalar.'

When set_index forms a MultiIndex (two or more source coordinates merged) onto a dimension d, every other variable of the object that was still dimensioned along one of the absorbed source-coordinate names (because that source coordinate had served as the variable's own dimension) has that dimension rewritten to the MultiIndex dimension d in the result; no retained variable keeps a dangling reference to a dimension name that has become a MultiIndex level.

When xarray.combine_by_coords is called with fill_value=None, each group of datasets (after being ordered from dimension coordinates) must create a complete hypercube; if datasets are missing such that the group does not form a complete hypercube, combine_by_coords raises a ValueError instead of returning a Dataset with missing/filled values.

"nanoseconds" is a recognized unit in TIME_UNITS, so netCDF timedelta variables whose attrs units == "nanoseconds" are decoded (CFTimedeltaCoder.decode takes the decode path and yields a numpy timedelta64[ns] array) instead of being returned undecoded.

In the plain-text repr of a DataArray or Variable (array_repr), when display_expand_data is False the data is rendered as the single-line inline_variable_array_repr summary instead of the (possibly multi-line) short_data_repr value shown when the option is True or left at 'default'.

duck_array_ops.is_duck_array (utils-level utility is_duck_array): an object that has ndim, shape and dtype attributes and implements __array_namespace__ counts as a duck array even when it does NOT provide both __array_function__ and __array_ufunc__; previously such an object was NOT a duck array.

AbstractArray.__format__ invoked with a non-empty format_spec on an array-valued (shape != ()) object raises NotImplementedError with a message stating that using format_spec is only supported when shape is () and reporting the actual shape.
