Converting to a pandas.Index an xarray Variable or DataArray whose underlying data is a pandas MultiIndex stored at a particular level (i.e. a MultiIndex level coordinate, such as a named level 'one' of a stacked dimension) yields a single-level, non-Multi pandas.Index of that level's values repeated per position, rather than the underlying full pandas MultiIndex of row tuples.

For each variable of the dataset, _protect_dataset_variables_inplace replaces the stored data with a CopyOnWriteArray wrapping of variable._data (itself wrapped in a MemoryCachedArray whenever the cache argument is truthy) exactly for those variables whose name is NOT a member of dataset._indexes; variables whose name IS one of the dataset's active indexes are skipped and left unmodified (their .data is never re-assigned).

When _config_initialization finds unrecognized command-line options still left in the parsed argument list (entries beginning with '-' or '--'), it no longer raises _UnrecognizedOptionError (and hence no longer causes an uncaught exception traceback); instead it delegates to the linter's argument parser error handling (linter._arg_parser.error), which presents the parser's usage/error message on stderr and terminates execution (argparse's exit-code-2 behavior under its default settings) rather than propagating an exception.

In expand_modules, while resolving a target given by module name, only an ImportError is swallowed and recorded as a fatal error entry; a SyntaxError raised during that resolution is no longer caught, so it propagates out of expand_modules instead of being added to the reported errors.

Invoking the pylint Run entry point with no file/package arguments (and with --version / pylint-config command handling not otherwise short-circuiting) prints the single line "No files to lint: exiting." to stdout and exits with code 32, instead of printing the full linter help text.

If the same option source (a configuration file or the command line) supplies both an enable/disable option that covers 'all' (value with a comma-separated element exactly 'all') and the opposite all-action option — i.e. both an '--enable=all'-type/--enable for all and an '--disable=all'-type/--disable for all — pylint raises pylint.config.exceptions.ArgumentPreprocessingError with the message '--enable=all and --disable=all are incompatible.' instead of silently choosing an order.

When warn_explicit_for's internal warnings.warn_explicit call raises a Warning (i.e. the warning has been escalated to an error, e.g. via -Werror or warnings-as-errors), warn_explicit_for re-raises an exception of the SAME type as the raised Warning whose message string is the original warning message followed by the offending method's location, "\n at <filename>:<lineno>", where <filename> is inspect.getfile(method) and <lineno> is method.__code__.co_firstlineno.

Assertion rewriting now gives assignment expressions (the walrus operator `:=`, ast.NamedExpr on Python >= 3.8) a dedicated visitor: a walrus that is part of a rewritten assertion's test is turned into an assignment that is snapshotted and described in the assertion's introspection, so a failing assertion whose condition contains a walrus produces an explanation that references the walrus's bound value/name like an ordinary variable, instead of the walrus falling through to generic handling that rewrites/mis-renders it.

on_rm_rf_error now accepts the calling convention used by shutil.rmtree(onexc=...), where its exception argument ('exc') is a bare BaseException instance, in addition to the legacy (type, exception, traceback) exc-info triple; under the bare-instance convention it discriminates errors with outcomes matching those for the triple form: a FileNotFoundError causes it to return False without warning, any other non-PermissionError exception causes it to emit a PytestWarning and return False, and a PermissionError reaching the deletion handling (chmod-and-retry vs. 'unknown function' warning) behaves as before.

_pytest.pytester_assertions.assert_outcomes: its `warnings` parameter is optional (default None); when it is None the assertion imposes no constraint on the actual warnings outcome count, and only when warned-parsed count is supplied explicitly (non-None) is the actual warnings count (parsed from the outcomes dict, defaulting to 0 if absent/not listed) required to equal it (mismatch makes the assertion fail).

When a confcutdir C is configured, conftest discovery treats a directory D as within confcutdir scope (so an ancestor conftest can be collected for it) if and only if D is not one of C's own ancestor/parent directories; only a directory strictly above C (a proper ancestor of C) is out of scope. In particular the confcutdir's own directory, its descendants, and directories that are unrelated to it (neither ancestors nor descendants of C, such as a sibling subtree) are all within scope.

Calling pytest.raises(expected_exception) with a falsy expected_exception (e.g. the empty tuple ()) immediately raises ValueError, raised by the raises() call itself before any code block runs or a context manager is returned, rather than deferring a less clear failure to context-exit or validation.

get_feature_names raises a ValueError with message of form "input_features should have length equal to number of features ({n_features}), got {given_length}" when a supplied input_features has length differing from the number of input features (len(self.categories_)).

_load_imgs (the JPEG-decoding step behind fetch_lfw_people and fetch_lfw_pairs) decodes each face JPEG and, when resize is not None, resizes it using sklearn/externals/_pilutil's imread and imresize, i.e. PIL/pillow-driven helpers rather than lazily imported scipy.misc.imread/imresize, so that face decoding requires only that Pillow be installed and no longer depends on scipy.misc and no scipy.misc DeprecationWarning is emitted.

In check_methods_subset_invariance, comparing a method's whole-set result with its per-sample results handles tuple-valued method outputs (e.g. some score_samples forms): only the first element of the returned tuple is used in the comparison, for both the whole-set call and each single-sample call.

The default value of the TfidfVectorizer.dtype parameter is np.float64 (rather than the integer np.int64 dtype inherited from CountVectorizer), so a TfidfVectorizer constructed without an explicit dtype stores dtype=np.float64.

Calling LabelEncoder.inverse_transform with an empty (0-sample) input on a fitted encoder returns an empty numpy array (np.array([])) rather than proceeding through the unseen-label validation and array indexing.

TfidfVectorizer.idf_ is writable: assigning an iterable of IDF weights to vectorizer.idf_ propagates them to the inner TfidfTransformer so that they become readable via vectorizer.idf_ and are used for weighting in transform(), overriding the need for them to be learned by fit().
FunctionTransformer's __init__ validate parameter defaults to None rather than True: an instance created without passing an explicit validate value has its validate attribute set to None.

After `fit`, SimpleImputer sets an `indicator_` attribute: when add_indicator=True it is a fitted sklearn.impute.MissingIndicator instance constructed with the imputer's own `missing_values` placeholder and trained on the fit-time data; when add_indicator=False it is None.

When GridSearchCV/RandomizedSearchCV.fit schedules fits over the product of the candidate params and the CV split iterator but zero individual fits are actually produced (e.g. the CV iterator yields no splits, or there are no candidates), fit raises a ValueError whose message reports that no fits were performed rather than proceeding to accumulate/format an empty result set.

When fit on training data where the requested n_quantiles exceeds the number of samples (n_samples), QuantileTransformer.fit issues a UserWarning reporting that n_quantiles is greater than the total number of samples and that n_quantiles is set to n_samples.

When GradientBoosting.fit is called with an explicit sample_weight and the init estimator's fit (as happens with an sklearn Pipeline) raises a ValueError whose message contains 'not enough values to unpack', a ValueError is raised whose message is 'The initial estimator <init.__class__.__name__> does not support sample weights.', chained from the original ValueError

Passing a discrete_features string that is not 'auto' (or that is not ExactlyEqual to the literal 'auto') raises a ValueError with message 'Invalid string value for discrete_features.', instead of being treated as a boolean-like or index-like value.

When analyzer is a callable and input is 'file' or 'filename', calling build_analyzer triggers a one-time validation probe in which the callable analyzer is invoked on the string name of a file that does not exist; if that invocation raises FileNotFoundError, or raises AttributeError with message "'str' object has no attribute 'read'", a warning classified as ChangedBehaviorWarning whose message begins 'Since v0.21, vectorizers pass the data to the custom analyzer...' is emitted; for any other outcome (the callable returns successfully or raises some other exception) no such ChangedBehaviorWarning is emitted and the exception is swallowed without propagating.

When VarianceThreshold.fit is called with the default threshold of 0.0 on sparse (CSR/CSC) input, any feature column whose samples are numerically constant across all rows is given an effective variance of 0 (self.variances_ = min(mean_variance_axis result, min_max_axis-derived range) = 0), so that the feature is dropped rather than being kept due to a floating-point residual variance.

AffinityPropagation.fit(X, y) with affinity='precomputed' and X a scipy sparse matrix raises an error during input validation (check_array with accept_sparse=False), rather than accepting the sparse matrix and storing it as affinity_matrix_.

_euclidean_distances_upcast accepts an optional batch_size argument (in addition to X, XX, Y, YY). When batch_size is None, its chunk size is auto-derived from the X/Y sparsity-based memory heuristic as before; when a batch_size value is supplied, that value is taken directly as the chunk size for batching over both X rows and Y rows (skipping the auto memory-based computation) and the remaining per-X-chunk Y-batch iteration proceeds using that chunk size.

For any normalization mode, divisions that would otherwise yield NaN (arising from a zero row, zero column, or zero total sum) are replaced with 0 in the returned confusion_matrix, rather than being surfaced as NaN/Inf entries (division operations are carried out with runtime floating-point errors suppressed).

_get_n_samples_bootstrap, when given a float (Real) max_samples, returns a count of round(n_samples * max_samples) that is never below 1: if round(n_samples * max_samples) would be 0, the returned number of bootstrap samples is 1.

Calling MLPClassifier.partial_fit or MLPRegressor.partial_fit (stochastic solver 'adam'/'sgd') on an estimator whose early_stopping parameter is True raises a ValueError with message "partial_fit does not support early_stopping=True", rather than continuing training. This applies regardless of whether the model was previously fit with early_stopping (which would leave best_loss_ = None) or is a first partial_fit call, and it occurs before validation-set splitting / weight initialization of the incremental pass.

kmeans_plusplus now exposes a new keyword-only parameter `sample_weight` (array-like of shape (n_samples,), default None, versionadded 1.3); when provided it is validated against X via _check_sample_weight (a malformed weight — e.g. negative values or length != n_samples — raises), and non-None weights are propagated into the private weighted seed-selection routine.

RocCurveDisplay.plot renders a legend at location 'lower right' whenever a label is present in the main ROC line's kwargs OR in the chance-level line's kwargs (so that when plot_chance_level=True the 'Chance level (AUC = 0.5)' line is always included in the legend); it renders no legend only when neither curve carries a label.

When fitting an AdaBoost* estimator whose estimator is not set and whose base_estimator is set to None, a FutureWarning is emitted whose message states that 'base_estimator' was renamed to 'estimator' in version 1.2 and will be removed in 1.4 (i.e. an explicitly-provided None base_estimator is treated as a deprecated use of the base_estimator parameter).

export_text accepts class_names given as any array-like (list, numpy array, and other array-like containers) of target-class labels; previously only a list was accepted. The provided names are used to label leaf classes in the returned report.

In BaseForest.fit, the unavailable-target check that raises ValueError ('The type of target cannot be used to compute OOB estimates...') for an OOB-unsupported y (multiclass-multioutput or unknown) is performed only when oob_score is set AND either new estimators were grown this call or the estimator lacks an oob_score_; a warm_start refit that grows no new trees on an already-OOB-computed estimator never raises this ValueError regardless of the supplied y's target type.

When PowerTransformer fits with method='box-cox' on data that contains a column (feature) consisting entirely of NaN values, the fit/fit_transform raises a ValueError (rather than attempting to compute the Box-Cox lambda on an empty non-NaN slice and failing with an unpacking error).

Both MLPClassifier and MLPRegressor accept a new `max_fun` constructor keyword argument (with default 15000) which is stored as the public instance attribute/estimator parameter `self.max_fun` and forwarded to the shared BaseMultilayerPerceptron initializer; it is visible through the estimator's parameter interface (get_params).

When the configured language is exactly 'en', Sphinx performs no catalog searching, mo-file compilation, or translator population from locale dirs (the translator is initialized with an empty locale list) and logs none of the 'loading translations...'/'done'/'not available for built-in messages' messages.

The hardcoded-extlink-detector external link checker does not emit its 'could be replaced by an extlink' replacement-suggestion warning when the captured value (the portion of the URI matching the extlink base pattern's %s capture) contains a forward slash '/', even if the URI otherwise matches an extlink base pattern with a non-empty value.

When rendering a `footnote` node that is tagged `referred` (i.e. it is referenced more than once, so the later references have been rewritten to `footnotemark` nodes by the LaTeXFootnoteTransform), the emitted LaTeX is a plain footnote environment that starts directly with `\begin{footnote}[<label>]\sphinxAtStartFootnote`, and the writer no longer prefixes that environment with a `\sphinxstepexplicit ` invocation and no longer inserts a `\phantomsection\label{\thesphinxscope.<label>}%` anchor (with its trailing comment-newline) inside the environment body.

When partitioning a docstring line into a leading part and its colon-separated description, a text run starting with the literal token ``:meta `` followed by further colon-delimited content (of shape `:meta KEY: VALUE...`, i.e. a ``:meta ...: ...`` construct) is treated as a single atomic/protected unit, so none of the colons inside it is taken as the leading/description boundary; text such as a ``:meta``-style embedded annotation on a parsed line is not split in the middle and remains attributed to the preceding field rather than being shifted into the description.

Description-typehints mode is driven by the autodoc_typehints config value staying equal to 'description' during the build (it is no longer internally rewritten to 'none' by a config-inited handler); description rendering no longer depends on any separately set runtime flag.

When autodoc_typehints == 'description' and a py object's contentnode is being transformed, if the contentnode's parent desc_signature node lacks the required context attributes (a missing 'module' and/or 'fullname', raising KeyError on attribute access), sphinx.ext.autodoc.typehints.merge_typehints must not propagate the KeyError to abort the build; instead it must cleanly return without modifying the contentnode or injecting any type-hint fields.
The mathjax_path configuration value, when not explicitly set by the user (i.e. left at its default), defaults to the string 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js'.
The man builder registers a confval named 'man_make_section_directory' whose default value is False.

A new Sphinx configuration value `autodoc_typehints_description_target` is registered with a default value of `'all'`, restricted to the two allowed values `'all'` and `'documented'` (Sphinx's enum validator rejects any other value), and flagged as an upgrade/rebuild-triggering setting.

The viewcode extension no longer inserts pending_xref nodes of reftype 'viewcode' into the doctree; nevertheless, any such pending_xref still reaching the missing_reference handler is resolved into a source reference link as before, and resolving one of these legacy nodes emits a RemovedInSphinx50Warning deprecation warning.

Setting up the `sphinx.ext.autodoc` extension now also sets up the `sphinx.ext.autodoc.preserve_defaults` sub-extension, which registers on the Sphinx application a configuration option named `autodoc_preserve_defaults` whose default is `False`.

When the linkcheck extension is set up (module setup()), the 'linkcheck-process-uri' event no longer registers rewrite_github_anchor as a handler, so github.com hrefs/fragments are no longer rewritten to prefix their fragment with 'user-content-' during hyperlink collection/checking; a github.com URL such as '.../sphinx#documentation' is collected and checked under its original fragment rather than being rewritten to '.../sphinx#user-content-documentation'.

The C domain DefinitionParser accepts as fundamental type specifiers the remaining GNU/standard-extension scalar keywords: the decimal '_Decimal32'/'_Decimal64'/'_Decimal128'; the integers '__uint128', '__int128', and (optionally 'signed'/'unsigned'-prefixed) '__int(8|16|32|64|128)'; and the floating/profile extensions '__float80', '_Float64x', '__float128', '_Float128', '__ibm128', '__fp16'.

Every pending_xref node produced by type_to_xref now carries a refspecific attribute (its value is True exactly when the incoming target began with a leading '.', and False otherwise); because PythonDomain.resolve_xref treats mere presence of the refspecific attribute as enabling refspecific search, all type-annotation cross-references emitted through type_to_xref (e.g. from py:data/py:attribute/py:property ':type:', function return/parameter annotations) are now resolved in refspecific search mode (module/class-context and suffix-based lookup) rather than the default exact-match mode even when the target is not prefixed.

LaTeX printing of a FormalPowerSeries (e.g. the object returned by fps(f)) renders the series' infinite Closed-form representation s.infinite — the Add of the independent terms plus an unevaluated \sum (sigma) over the general term ak.formula * xk.formula running from k=ak.start to infinity — instead of the truncated finite polynomial expansion returned by s.truncate(). Concretely, latex(fps(f)) now contains an infinite Sum over the coefficient/general term and no longer trails the truncated 6-term expansion with a \mathcal{O}(...) order term.

CCodePrinter now prints Relational expressions (Eq, Ne, Gt, Lt, Ge, Le) as an inline infix C comparison '<lhs_code> <rel_op> <rhs_code>' with the C operator token and surrounding spaces (for example 'x != 0', 'x == c') instead of falling back to StrPrinter's representation (which rendered == ' as 'Eq(...)' and '!=' as 'Ne(...)').

Arguments passed to _print_Or that bind less tightly than Or (e.g. nested conjunction operands) are wrapped in parentheses so disjunctions of conjunctions print e.g. '(x & ~y) | (y & ~x)' and disjunctions over multiple relationals print each <relational>-conjunction in parentheses, preserving the disjunction's operands as distinct grouped terms.

When factorint(n, multiple=True) yields a factorization in which an entry has non-positive multiplicity (a case reachable only when n's inputs introduce denominator primes, e.g. factor-rich Mul/dict composite inputs), that entry is represented in the returned list by S(1)/p repeated |multiplicity| times rather than by an integer p; otherwise positive-multiplicity entries remain integers p.

Matrix.is_upper_hessenberg evaluates to True for a rectangular matrix having more rows than columns whose entries that lie in the strictly-below-subdiagonal band within the matrix's actual columns are all zero — in particular an all-zero k×m matrix with k > m reports is_upper_hessenberg == True rather than raising an IndexError from iterating a column index ≥ cols.

An Add that is a pure complex 'number' r + i*I with r, i rational and with D = sqrt(r^2 + i^2) rational (a Pythagorean triple) evaluates a Rational power whose denominator (q) is 2 (e.g. the square root) to the closed principal-branch algebraic form sqrt((D - r)/2)^p * ((D + r)/abs(i) + sign(i)*I)^p (with the p-th power of the inner binomial expanded), rather than remaining an unevaluated radical; e.g. sqrt(3 + 4*I) yields the exact reduced value.

When the first argument is a Poly with exactly one generator and k is a positive Integer (with x finite and not +/-oo), RisingFactorial.eval returns the expanded functional product of the shifted polynomial, i.e. x(y)*x(y+1)*...*x(y+k-1) as a Poly (e.g. rf(Poly(x**3, x), 2) -> Poly(x**6 + 3*x**5 + 3*x**4 + x**3, x, domain='ZZ')).

When expr is an Add expression and separate=True, decompose returns a Python set (unordered, duplicate-free) whose elements are the constituent monomials of expr (one per Add term), instead of a list.

For an Add or Mul instance whose `as_independent(Symbol, AppliedUndef)` yields a non-identity numeric part x and a non-trivial tail (the "pure number" path of AssocOp._eval_evalf), `_eval_evalf(prec)` returns the freshly-constructed flat expression `self.func(x, e1, e2, ...)` where each `ei` is the individual result of that tail argument's own `_eval_evalf(prec)` (the original tail argument kept when its `_eval_evalf` returns None); this reconstruction is performed unconditionally on every call, rather than only when the per-tail-argument evaluations actually changed something.

Calling the module-level sympy.polys.polytools.degree on a non-Poly, non-numeric Expr that has more than one distinct free symbol raises type-errors.TypeError when no explicit symbolic generator is supplied (i.e. when the gen argument is numeric, including its default value 0), instead of returning the degree with respect to the canonically-chosen first generator.

The simplify() signature is changed so that the former fourth keyword parameter `fu` is removed and replaced by a new keyword `rational` (default False), i.e. the signature is simplify(expr, ratio=1.7, measure=count_ops, rational=False); consequently a call that passes an explicit `fu=...` keyword now raises TypeError and a call passing `rational=...` (True, False, or None) is accepted.
For an argument z known to be real, sinh(z).is_positive equals z.is_positive (True iff z is positive real); for non-real z it is not asserted.

The sinc class no longer subclasses TrigonometricFunction; sinc is instead a direct subclass of Function. Consequently a sinc(...) instance is not an instance of TrigonometricFunction (whereas previously sinc(x).__class__ was a TrigonometricFunction with sinc being a sinc instance), while it remains an ordinary Function/Expr.
rcode / RCodePrinter translates a factorial function expression into an R call 'factorial(...)' of its argument, rather than reporting it as not supported.

The negative-base, negative-exponent simplification in both Rational._eval_power and Integer._eval_power no longer branches on whether the negative exponent is an integer (expt.q == 1): a single representation is returned for all negative non-unit exponents, with the sign factored as (-1)**expt using the untransformed negative exponent.

When JuliaCodePrinter prints a Mul whose factors include a Pow with exponent exactly -1 whose base is itself a Mul holding more than one factor, the Julia division denominator text for that base (which uses elementwise './' 'as appropriate') is wrapped in parentheses so that the denominator product is grouped rather than left as a bare product after the division operator.

In the unicode path of _print_BasisDependent, when reassembling a newline-containing coefficient, the branch that re-inserts the basis vector label is chosen by which parenthesis glyph the stripped coefficient text contains: if it contains the `\N{right parenthesis extension}` glyph (a vertically-extended/fraction-height rendering), the label is inserted exactly once immediately after the first occurrence of that glyph (the loop breaks after the first insertion), instead of being duplicated after every parenthesis hook on every line of the tall rendering.

ConditionSet's third argument base_set is optional, defaulting to S.UniversalSet, so ConditionSet(sym, condition) (with no base set) constructs a ConditionSet whose .base_set is S.UniversalSet instead of raising a TypeError.

binomial(n, k) auto-evaluates to n when n - k equals 1 (i.e. k == n - 1) and n is known to be nonnegative or a non-integer; in particular, binomial(n, n - 1) now evaluates to n for a positive-integer symbol n instead of remaining unevaluated.

CodePrinter._print_Function treats an applied Function whose name is not among the printer's known_functions and which has no inlined `_imp_` Lambda conditionally: when it satisfies expr.is_Function and the printer's `allow_unknown_functions` setting is truthy, it is emitted as a literal call of the form `<printed func>(<printed arg1>, <printed arg2>, …)` (the function name and each argument printed recursively, comma-joined with ', ') instead of being routed to _print_not_supported; when `allow_unknown_functions` is False (or expr.is_Function is false) such a Function is still recorded as Not supported and returned via the pre-existing fallback.

FCodePrinter (e.g. via fcode) raises NotImplementedError when asked to print a SymPy Mod / % expression while the 'standard' setting is 66 or 77 (the raised message states that Python's % operator and SymPy's Mod() are not supported by Fortran 66 or 77); since the default 'standard' is 77, a plain fcode(Mod(...)) now raises.

In periodicity(f, symbol), when f is a Mod whose argument a is neither symbol itself nor a TrigonometricFunction, the linear-period shortcut returning Abs(n/a.diff(symbol)) is used only when a is a polynomial in symbol (and degree(a, symbol)==1 and symbol is not in the free symbols of the Mod modulus n); for a Mod argument a that is not a polynomial in symbol, this shortcut is no longer taken.
srepr(S.Integers) (ReprPrinter._print_Integers) returns the string 'Integers' rather than the emptyPrinter fallback 'Integers()'.
For a power with a base known to be zero and an exponent known to be real, Pow.is_negative always returns False (a zero base to any real exponent is never negative).

LatexPrinter now prints a HadamardPower (elementwise matrix power) matrix expression instead of falling through to a generic constructor-style print: the base is printed with the standard power-handling used for ordinary x**n superscripts and the exponent is shown as an elementwise (ring)∘ marker, yielding output of the form `{base}^{\circ {<exp>}}` (e.g. a bare MatrixSymbol base printed as `A^{\circ {2}}`).

For a Segment3D or Ray3D argument whose intersection with the plane is empty (the entity does not reach the plane), Plane.distance returns the Euclidean distance from the plane to the nearest point actually on that bounded/ray entity rather than the perpendicular plane-to-point distance to that entity's first defining point regardless of its extent: for a Ray3D this is the plane-to-point distance of the ray's initial point o.p1, and for a Segment3D it is the plane-to-point distance of the nearer of the two endpoints.

A new physical constant named `elementary_charge`, with symbol/abbreviation "e", of electric-charge dimension (`charge`), and numeric scale factor `1.602176634e-19 * coulomb`, is defined and exported from the `sympy.physics.units` namespace (accessible as `u.elementary_charge`).

Range accepts symbolic start/stop/step arguments (an argument that contains a Symbol and is not known to be non-integer, or is infinite) instead of raising ValueError; e.g. Range(i, j, k) with pure symbols constructs successfully and its .start/.stop/.step expose the supplied symbolic values (no literal-integer requirement). Finite literal non-integer arguments (e.g. pi) are still rejected with the 'Finite arguments to Range must be integers' ValueError.

When IndexedBase is constructed from a string label together with assumptions passed as keyword arguments, the Symbol stored as the resulting label (args[0] / label property) is created with exactly those assumptions, so the label itself carries the assumption set (e.g. IndexedBase('A', real=True).label.is_real is True and the label is the Symbol 'A' with the real assumption).
A sign expression whose argument is known to be zero under the assumptions refines to 0 (IntegerZero / S.Zero).

Expr equality (__eq__) against a Python native string returns False regardless of the string text (e.g. Symbol('x') == 'x' is False and Integer(1) == '1' is False), rather than sympify-parsing the string content and comparing against it (which could otherwise make Symbol('x') == 'x' evaluate to True).

Under evaluation-disabled context (evaluate(False)), adding (or the reflected add of) oo or -oo with any Number operand no longer collapses to the eager infinite/NaN result (nan/oo/-oo); instead it produces an unevaluated Add expression (e.g. Add(oo, -1) rather than oo).
S.Rationals.boundary equals S.Reals (the whole real line), rather than Rationals itself.

For such an integer-ImageSet vs. Integers/imageSet intersection, when f(n)=g(m) admits exactly one parametric (infinite) solution family for n with a single free symbol, the intersection is returned as the ImageSet { f(h(t)) : t in Integers } with the resulting lambda expression expanded.

latex() accepts a new optional boolean keyword argument parenthesize_super, defaulting to True, and forwards it into the LatexPrinter configuration; the LatexPrinter's default settings likewise define parenthesize_super to True (so a printer constructed without that setting also behaves as True).
SchurNumber(S.Infinity) evaluates (via eval) to S.Infinity.

SciPyPrinter._print_airyai maps a SymPy airyai function to the string 'scipy.special.airy(<printed arg>)[0]', where <printed arg> is the printer's rendering of the function's single argument (index 0 of scipy.special.airy, corresponding to Ai).
dup_zz_mignotte_bound returns the non-negative even integer bound; for the polynomial `f = x**3 + 14*x**2 + 56*x + 64` over the integer domain ZZ it returns exactly 152.

collect(expr, syms, evaluate=False), when syms contains a nonsymbol (an expression that is neither a Symbol nor -Symbol nor contains a Wild), returns a dict in which each value (the collected coefficient/Add expression for a key) has had the internal Dummy placeholders substituted back to the original input symbols, i.e. the coefficient values are expressed in terms of the caller's original syms/expr symbols and contain no leaked temporary Dummy variables. (Keys were already mapped back before this change; now values are mapped back too.)

In LatexPrinter._print_Pow, when the expression is a Pow whose base is a commutative Rational unit-fraction (base.p * base.q == abs(base.q)) and whose negative rational exponent is not -1, the LaTeX emitted is \frac{1}{(\frac{p}{q})^{m}} where p,q are the base's stored numerator/denominator and m is the absolute value of the negative exponent (e.g. rendering Pow(Rational(1,2), -2, evaluate=False) as '\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2})^{2}}'), rather than routing through _print_Mul.

When a MatMul consists of two factors, one being a MatAdd matrix expression and the other a Rational scalar, canonicalization (MatMul.doit/canonicalize) now distributes the scalar over the MatAdd rather than leaving the scalar-times-sum as an unevaluated product. That is, the product of the Rational `r` with the MatAdd of terms, written in either factor order (scalar before the sum or after the sum), evaluates to a MatAdd of the scalar applied to each term individually; e.g. `r*(A+B)` (and the reversed-order form) evaluates to `r*A + r*B`, each `r*term` result itself being passed through doit.

Rendering a SingularityFunction that itself carries an outer exponent (a powered SingularityFunction, i.e. one printed through the LaTeX Pow path that supplies an `exp`) does not raise an error and yields the wrapped LaTeX form `{\left({\langle SHIFT \rangle}^{POWER}\right)}^{EXP}`, where SHIFT is the rendered argument-difference (args[0]-args[1]), POWER is the rendered internal exponent (args[2]), and EXP is the rendered outer exponent.

Constructing a symbolic Range collapses it to the canonical empty range (start=stop=0, step=1, i.e. Range(0)) whenever the computed member count (stop-start)/step is exactly 0 (start and stop symbolically equal) or is negative (a symbolically-descending or vacuous span), rather than merely detecting the trivial start==stop case.

When Factors is constructed from an Expr whose power decomposition already has an entry keyed by the imaginary unit I and whose commutative argument list also contains standalone I atoms (whose count i was removed from the args), the resulting I entry in the factors dict is the sum of the pre-existing I-entry exponent and i — the pre-existing I exponent is not clobbered/replaced by i.

Each value in the relations dict passed to the CoordSystem constructor must, per stored (source-system-name, target-system-name) key, carry both the source system's coordinate symbols and the target's transformed-coordinate expressions: canonicalization stores an entry as the 2-tuple (tuple-of-source-symbols, tuple-of-target-expressions). A Lambda value is converted using its signature and expr; any other value has element [0] taken as the source-symbols tuple and element [1] as the target-expressions tuple.

When the domain of a DDM is a RealField (RR) or ComplexField (CC), DDM.rref selects each pivot by row-pivoting within the column: among the not-yet-processed rows it chooses the one whose entry has the largest absolute value, using that row as the pivot row before continuing with the standard elimination; matrices over these inexact fields are therefore reduced correctly and the returned reduced-row-echelon form and pivot list match a properly row-pivoted RREF rather than picking an accidentally small leading entry as the pivot.
LaTeX printing of a single-argument LambertW raised to a power produces the exponent as a superscript attached to the W symbol: W^{n}\left(z\right) where n is the printed exponent.

Mul.is_integer reports False (not None/undecidable) for products where the remaining (post-±1-removal) numerator factors are all odd while at least one denominator factor is even, and for forms having a single even numerator Integer whose combined factor-of-2 content from the even denominators strictly exceeds the numerator's own factor-of-2 count.

When a denominator-only unevaluated Mul has exactly one denominator factor, the printed numerator is the literal '1' and the result takes the single-factor form '1/<denominator>' (no enclosing parentheses); when it has more than one denominator factor the result takes the multi-factor form '1/(<d1>*<d2>...)' with parenthesized denominator.

For f an instance of Min or Max containing the decomposition symbol, when every symbol-containing argument of f has a decompogen whose trailing elements (all elements after the first, after an argument that itself yields exactly one decomposition element is treated as if it decomposed as [symbol, arg]) are mutually identical, decompogen(f, symbol) returns [Min_or_Max_same_type] + [that common trailing sequence], where the rebuilt Min/Max preserves the same type (Min stays Min, Max stays Max) and the same positions/values of symbol-free arguments, with each symbol-containing argument position replaced by the first element of that argument's own decompogen.

UnitSystem._collect_factor_and_dimension still returns, as the factor (first) component of a Function expression, the expression's .func applied to the collected scale factors of its arguments (this wrapping of factors is unchanged); only the dimension component is no longer wrapped in the function.

pow_rep_recursive, when asked to select exactly one more term (k == 1) to complete the remaining amount n_remaining, resolves that final term directly instead of recursing further: it emits the tuple terms + (r,) where r is the exact p-th integer root of n_remaining, and emits that tuple only if n_remaining is an exact p-th power (r^p == n_remaining) and r <= n_i; if n_remaining is not an exact p-th power or its exact root exceeds n_i it yields nothing, and in every k == 1 case the generator returns immediately rather than descending more recursion frames for that term.

MathematicaParser._from_mathematica_to_tokens tokenizes a comment-cleaned code split with the tokenizer regex (tokenizer.findall) only when that split is a str and is all-ASCII; a str split containing any non-ASCII character (e.g. a Greek letter such as λ) is instead appended to the returned token list as a single opaque token equal to the whole split, so the non-ASCII characters are preserved rather than silently dropped by findall. (Equivalently, the two cases that previously took the tokenizer route — a plain ASCII split and a non-ASCII split — now differ: the latter is not fragmented.)
In the cgs_gauss unit system, the scale factor of ampere is set to 10*speed_of_light*statcoulomb/second.
Multiplying two Prefixes whose scale factors are reciprocal (scale product == 1) yields S.One (a SymPy Integer equal to 1) rather than the bare Python integer 1, e.g. m*k == 1 still holds.

The ITRS frame carries an EarthLocation 'location' frame attribute whose default is the centre of the Earth, so an ITRS frame/coordinate can be created (or defaulted) with either an explicit topocentric (non-geocentric) observing site or, by default, the geocenter, and it can be transformed to a topocentric ITRS that is offset from the geocenter.

_line_type recognizes the missing-value token 'NO' and the 'nan' data token case-insensitively during line classification: a row consisting of multiple NO tokens in any letter case (e.g. 'no no no no') is still classified as 'new' (a table separator), and a data row whose values include NO/nan in mixed or lowercase casing (e.g. '1.2 no' or 'NAN') is classified as a data line of the correct column count rather than rejected as unrecognized.

_format_float(value) always returns a string of length at most 20: when the base representation exceeds 20 characters and contains scientific notation ('E'), only the leading mantissa characters are dropped so the retained prefix plus the intact 'E' exponent portion totals 20 characters; when the base representation exceeds 20 characters and contains no 'E', the first 20 characters are returned.

Header.fromstring accepts a `bytes` first argument (in addition to `str`) and builds a Header whose parsed cards are equivalent to parsing the latin-1 decoding of those bytes; arbitrary byte values (including non-ASCII, which latin-1 always decodes) are accepted without raising a TypeError/UnicodeDecodeError, with bytes passed onward to Card.fromstring for card parsing.

When Quantity is constructed from an existing Quantity input (no unit change) with dtype=None and copy=True, an integer-kind input Quantity is promoted to float64, whereas a float16 (or other float-kind) input Quantity keeps its original float dtype instead of being widened to float64 — only integer-kind inputs trigger the float default in this code path.

parse_duration, when matching the standard 'HH:MM:SS[.ffffff]' format, accepts an optional single leading '-' sign placed immediately before the time portion (before the hours term, or before the first term when there is no hours term), and that sign, when present, negates the entire time portion as a whole rather than only its leading (hours) term — e.g. "-01:02:03" yields a timedelta equal to negative (1 hour, 2 minutes, 3 seconds).

Under Oracle, when USE_TZ is enabled, _convert_field_to_tz (used by datetime_cast_date_sql, datetime_cast_time_sql, datetime_extract_sql, and datetime_trunc_sql) treats the stored datetime field as being in the connection's configured timezone: when self.connection.timezone_name differs from the requested tzname the SQL takes the field as being in the connection timezone (FROM_TZ source = self.connection.timezone_name, replacing the fixed '0:00' UTC offset) and converts it to tzname, and when the two timezones are equal the field is returned unchanged without any conversion.

In django.utils.numberformat.format, the zero-normalization applied to Decimals smaller than the decimal_pos cutoff discards the sign: a Decimal with magnitude below the cutoff produces the unsigned string (e.g. format(Decimal('-1e-200'), '.', decimal_pos=2) yields '0.00' with no leading minus), because the value is reset to a positive Decimal zero before the sign/negative handling.

UUIDField.get_prep_value coerces input through UUIDField.to_python: a non-uuid.UUID string-hexadecimal or integer value is converted into the corresponding uuid.UUID instance (so that a call such as pk.get_prep_value(<string object_id>) yields a uuid.UUID comparable to a UUID primary-key value), an already-uuid.UUID value and None are returned unchanged, and an unparseable value raises the same ValidationError as to_python.

When running the psql subprocess via runshell_db, if conn_params contains a truthy 'sslmode' value, the subprocess environment (passed as env= to subprocess.run) has its 'PGSSLMODE' variable set to str(sslmode); if the parameter is absent or falsey, 'PGSSLMODE' is not injected into the environment.

django.utils.html.escape(text) returns a SafeString whose content is the input str(text) with HTML-significant characters encoded, namely: & becomes &, < becomes <, > becomes >, " becomes ", and ' becomes '.

Field.get_choices returns a relation's related objects in the related model's default ordering (the ordering of its default manager, i.e. its Meta.ordering) when the 'ordering' argument is empty/() — instead of stripping that default ordering by appending a blank order_by() — and orders them by the supplied non-empty 'ordering' fields when such are given.

URL resolution through regex-based patterns (re_path/url, via RegexPattern.match) excludes from the resolved kwargs any named capture group whose value is None (i.e., an optional named group in the regex that did not participate in the match). Such an unmatched optional group no longer appears as a keyword argument with value None; it is dropped from the match's kwargs entirely.

The cached hostname exposed by django.core.mail.utils DNS_NAME (CachedDnsName) is returned in punycoded ASCII form: get_fqdn() returns punycode(socket.getfqdn()) and __str__() yields that same ASCII form, so a non-ASCII system hostname is rendered as its `xn--` ACE label while an ASCII hostname is returned unchanged.

replace_unnamed_groups replaces an unnamed capture group that terminates the regex pattern at its very end (its closing ')' is the last character, with no following literal token, including nested groups such as '((x|y)\w+)') with '<var>'. E.g. '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/(\w+)' is returned as '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/<var>' and '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/((x|y)\w+)' as '^(?P<a>\w+)/b/<var>'.
EnumSerializer.serialize() returns the imports set {'import <module>'} for the enum member's module, without including any imports that serializing the member's underlying value would require.

During the same Model._check_ordering relation-path walk, once a path segment resolves to a field that is not a relation, the walk no longer treats any subsequent segment as a field of the model owned by the enclosing relation path (in the buggy code _cls kept that model and a later segment matching one of its real field names was silently accepted); a further segment after a non-relation field is now acceptable only if it resolves as a registered transform/lookup of that non-relation field, and if it cannot, that ordering entry produces an E015 error.

Calling str() on any member of a Choices-derived enum class (Choices itself, IntegerChoices, TextChoices, or a user subclass) returns the string form of that member's value (str(member.value)) rather than the standard enum string form that names the member, e.g. 'MyEnum.MEMBER_NAME' or the enum class reference.

When resolve_lookup_value is given a list/tuple whose elements are themselves lists/tuples, the nested iterables are resolved recursively and each nested level likewise preserves its own container type (list stays list, tuple stays tuple) across all nesting depths, rather than only the outermost level being handled.

Assigning a value to the pk attribute on a multi-table-inheritance (concrete-parent) model instance, in addition to setting the instance's own local primary-key attribute, also sets the instance attribute for the remote (parent) pk of every parent link registered in _meta.parents whose field is not the model's own primary-key field to that same assigned value. Non-parent-linked, single-table models are unaffected: pk assignment still only sets the local pk attribute.

ModelChoiceField: When a ModelChoiceField uses a RadioSelect widget but the field does allow blank (blank argument is True), the leading empty/blank choice is retained (empty_label stays equal to the supplied empty_label, defaulting to '---------'), so an empty radio option is still rendered.

Query.output_field, when len(self.select) == 1 and the single select expression exposes a 'target' attribute that is truthy (e.g. a Col selecting a concrete column), returns that element's 'target' field rather than the element's own 'field'/output field.

During CombinedExpression.resolve_expression, a combined arithmetic expression whose two operands resolve to different field internal types where at least one is DurationField (a DurationField mixed with a non-duration field) is rewritten, at resolution time, into a DurationExpression and recursively resolved; the rewritten DurationExpression is resolved as a duration-arithmetic expression on every backend rather than only on backends lacking a native duration field.

When ordering two Field instances with equal creation_counters: an unattached field (no model) orders before a model-attached field; two fields both attached to models are ordered by comparing their models' (app_label, model_name) tuples; two unattached fields with equal counters are not strictly ordered relative to one another.

On POSIX systems, locks.lock() returns False (does not raise) when the flock call fails with BlockingIOError, i.e. when a non-blocking (LOCK_NB) lock attempt is denied due to contention; exceptions other than BlockingIOError propagate.

When display_for_field is called with a value that is truthy and a field that is a models.JSONField, the returned text is the JSON serialization of that value in which non-ASCII characters appear as literal characters rather than as \uXXXX escapes (serialized with python json.dumps using ensure_ascii=False and the field's encoder); on a serialization TypeError it still falls back to display_for_value(value, empty_value_display).

Frame generation for each contributing exception skips traceback frames whose frame locals set __traceback_hide__ to a truthy value, and otherwise reports every frame of that exception's traceback in tb_next order; the last reported frame of the whole list corresponds to the last non-hidden frame reached.

When a lazy proxy value appears on the LEFT-hand side of the addition operator (evaluated as ``<lazy_proxy> + <other>``), the lazy proxy is forced to its concrete value and the operation's result is ``<cast concrete value> + <other>`` (delegating to the concrete value's ``__add__``) rather than raising a TypeError.

ThreadedWSGIServer's __init__ accepts an optional keyword argument connections_override (defaulting to None) and stores the passed value unchanged on the instance as the attribute connections_override.

Q.deconstruct() no longer special-cases a single non-Q child by re-encoding it into keyword kwargs: for a Q built from a single lookup keyword (single two-element child, e.g. Q(name='x')), the child is now returned as an element of the positional args (args=(('name','x'),)) with an empty kwargs dict, rather than as args=() with kwargs={'name':'x'}.

BaseDatabaseOperations.year_lookup_bounds_for_date_field gains an optional iso_year keyword flag; when iso_year=True the returned [lower, upper] pair spans the ISO-8601 week-numbering year equal to value, not the calendar year value — the lower bound is the day on which ISO week 1 of value begins, and the upper bound is the last day of that ISO week-numbering year (the day before ISO week 1 of value+1 begins), each still passed through the same date-value adaptation used by the calendar path.

The `-m` relaunch branch is now selected based solely on __main__.__spec__ being present (not None); it is no longer additionally gated on a truthy __main__.__spec__.parent, so when __spec__ exists but parent is empty the child is still relaunched via `python -m <name>` rather than falling through to the script-file path.

BaseDatabaseClient.runshell invokes the client executable via subprocess.run with env=None (so the child inherits the calling process's os.environ) whenever settings_to_cmd_args_env returns a falsy env value such as an empty dict, instead of passing that empty dict/env to the subprocess.

URLValidator raises a ValidationError (message 'Enter a valid URL.', code 'invalid', params {'value': value}) when the value is a str that contains any tab ('\t'), carriage-return ('\r'), or line-feed ('\n') character, and this rejection happens even when the same value would otherwise have been accepted by the trivial regex or by the IDN retry path.

settings_to_cmd_args_env() resolves the database name for the mysql CLI from settings_dict['OPTIONS']['database'] when present, falling back to settings_dict['OPTIONS']['db'] and then to settings_dict['NAME'] (i.e. the OPTIONS 'database' key is now accepted as an alias); when the resolved value is non-empty it is appended as the final positional (database) argument in the returned command args.

BoundWidget.id_for_label returns the value of the 'id' key in the subwidget's data['attrs'] dictionary, i.e. the id attribute that will actually be rendered on that option/input; when data['attrs'] contains no 'id' entry (e.g. the form has auto_id disabled and the widget's own attrs specify no id), it returns None rather than fabricating an id string from the widget name and index.
QuerySet.bulk_update() called with an empty collection of objects (objs with no elements, after all field/pk validation has passed) returns the integer 0 rather than returning None.

When the value being serialized by TypeSerializer (via serializer_factory / MigrationWriter.serialize) is exactly the models.Model class type (identity match in the special_cases list), the serialization result is the string 'models.Model' with the import set {'from django.db import models'}, so that this import is propagated into the writer's imports and a generated migration referencing models.Model (e.g. as a CreateModel base) ends up importing models from django.db.

When BaseFormSet.full_clean() runs and no formset-level ValidationError is caught (including when the formset is unbound / management form is invalid / all checks pass), the non-form error list it produces and that formset.non_form_errors() returns is an ErrorList whose error_class is 'errorlist nonform', so rendering it as HTML (as_ul()/str()) emits '<ul class="errorlist nonform">'.

modelformset_factory(model, ...) accepts an `edit_only` keyword argument that defaults to False, and the FormSet class it returns exposes a class attribute `edit_only` whose value equals the `edit_only` argument passed in.
django.utils.timezone._get_timezone_name(tz) returns the result of tz.tzname(None) when that call yields a truthy (non-None, non-empty) string, and otherwise falls back to returning str(tz).

get_language_from_path() recognizes a path whose initial language-prefix segment is a code of the form word('-word|@word){0,2} — i.e. comprised of up to three subtags joined by single '-' or '@' (e.g. en-latn-us, zh-hant-tw) — extracting that whole three-subtag code as the candidate language code; for a path prefix representing a supported language (present in LANGUAGES and with a matching locale file), it returns the corresponding supported language variant instead of None. (Previously only one- and two-subtag prefixes such as en, en-us, pt-br could be parsed; a three-subtag prefix such as en-latn-us caused the code not to be extracted.)

When migrate() is invoked with an explicit empty plan (plan == []) and the django_migrations table does not exist on the migration connection's database, migrate() returns the ProjectState built from the unmigrated apps (with_applied_migrations=False) without creating the django_migrations table (i.e. it performs an early return before ensure_schema/table creation and before folding applied migrations into the state).

The base Field class exposes a per-field-class attribute `non_db_attrs` (a tuple of attribute names whose change does not affect a column definition and thus is ignored when deciding whether a field alteration is needed). Its default value includes blank, choices, db_column, editable, error_messages, help_text, limit_choices_to, on_delete, related_name, related_query_name, validators, and verbose_name; standard field subclasses inherit it. A custom field subclass may override/extend `non_db_attrs` to declare which of its deconstruct keyword attributes are non-schema-affecting.

ForeignKey.db_parameters(connection) returns a dict that, in addition to 'type' and 'check', contains a 'collation' key whose value is the value returned under 'collation' by the foreign key's target_field.db_parameters(connection).

When RenameIndex.database_forwards resolves the pre-renaming (from-state / actually-present) index and that index's name already equals self.new_name — i.e. the operation is a no-op because nothing would change — it performs no database schema change (does not call schema_editor.rename_index, and does not require the to_state index lookup) and returns normally, rather than attempting to rename an index to a name it already carries (which previously triggered a duplicate-relation error on re-application of an unnamed-index rename after its no-op backward step).

When a defer()/only() column spec traverses an intermediate relation whose target model is a proxy model, Query.deferred_to_data registers the required pk/reference fields under the proxy's concrete backing model (so the concrete model's pk column is included among the selected/loaded columns), and the resulting query loads and populates the related (proxy) object with its pk correctly set rather than failing during object population because the pk column is missing.

On any path where floatformat cannot produce a formatted result and echoes the input value back unmodified (i.e. when arg is not a valid integer magnitude, or when the value cannot be processed as a Decimal), a Decimal input is echoed as its plain digit string (str form), e.g. '555.555', rather than as its repr Python-literal form "Decimal('555.555')".

When.as_sql: when the condition compiles to an empty SQL string (a filter that matches every row, e.g. a negated empty lookup like ~Q(pk__in=[])), the CASE WHEN branch is emitted with an always-true predicate as its condition instead of a malformed/empty condition — so the WHEN's THEN result is returned for every row.

A `%` (MOD connector) CombinedExpression whose operands are an Integer output field and a Float output field (in either order) no longer raises FieldError during output-field resolution; its inferred output type is FloatField.
The --check option help text states that it exits with a non-zero status when model changes are missing migrations and that it does not actually write the migration files.

get_aggregation decides whether to route the aggregate through the subquery-wrapping path based on whether existing annotations actually involve aggregate/window computation: it uses a subquery only if some existing selected annotation contains an aggregate or an OVER clause, or if some existing filter references an aggregate/window alias (a HAVING/QUALIFY condition); the mere presence of pre-existing annotations that are neither is no longer sufficient to force a subquery.

When ServerHandler processes a HEAD request and the WSGI application's response set a Content-Length header, that Content-Length header is removed before the response is finalized, so the HEAD response does not advertise a body length derived from the (stripped) payload.

A constraint whose `violation_error_code` is not None is deconstructed (and thus cloned) with that `violation_error_code` included in kwargs, so `clone()` reproduces the non-default code; the kwarg is omitted when the code is None (the default).

When FileResponse serves a compressed file whose basename ends in '.br' and no explicit content_type is provided, the response's Content-Type header is set to 'application/x-brotli' (rather than the guessed type such as text/*).

SelectDateWidget.value_from_datadict does not raise OverflowError when the submitted year/month/day values are integers that cause datetime.date(int(y), int(m), int(d)) to raise OverflowError (rather than ValueError); instead it returns the string "0-0-0".

The above cancellation matches purely on the index name (self.index.name == operation.name) without constraining that the paired RemoveIndex targets the same model as the AddIndex or that it immediately follows it, so an AddIndex is also cancelled by a RemoveIndex naming that index even when the two operations name different models and/or have other operations in between.

Elements of the input sequence that are already marked safe (SafeString/SafeData instances or objects exposing an HTML representation via `__html__`) are included in the returned list unchanged with no double-escaping applied.

When serializing in pk format (serializer invoked without natural keys) an object that has an auto-created many-to-many field whose target model's default manager carries a select_related on its queryset, the XML serializer (django.core.serializers.xml_serializer.Serializer) succeeds in iterating the m2m relations and emits one <object pk=...> reference per related object, rather than raising the 'Field ... cannot be both deferred and traversed using select_related at the same time' error.

Calling Axes.set_xlim with a reversed (descending) request on a log-scaled x-axis — e.g. ax.set_xlim(x_max, x_min) where the first argument > the second — produces an inverted (descending) x view interval instead of being silently re-sorted ascending by log-scale limit adjustment: afterwards get_xlim()/viewLim.intervalx returns its two values with the first greater than the second and ax.xaxis_inverted() == True. Normal ascending calls (first argument < second) still yield a non-inverted ascending interval.

When an interactive (interactive=True) vertical SpanSelector is created, the two initial edge-handle artist lines are placed at data y-positions equal to the axes' current y-axis data limits (ax.get_ybound()), rather than at the initially-zero selector extents; consequently constructing the selector leaves the axes' y view limits unchanged (does not autoscale them, in particular does not expand them toward data coordinate 0 when 0 lies outside the data view).
Constructing a Legend whose parent is neither an Axes nor a FigureBase raises TypeError with the exact message 'Legend needs either Axes or FigureBase as parent'.

When _wrap_in_tex converts its input text into TeX math-mode wrapping (used for usetex-rendered date tick labels), every colon ':' character that survives the earlier letter-classification step is braced as '{:}' in the returned string, so that time separators are not typeset with the wide spacing TeX gives to binary/relation operators.

UnitData.update invoked with empty data does not emit the INFO-level log message 'Using categorical units to plot a list of strings that are all parsable as floats or dates...' (the message is suppressed when data is empty even though the all-convertible check is vacuously true).

In ConciseDateFormatter.format_ticks, when the finest tick level whose values vary across the given ticks is at the year (level 0) or month (level 1) field, the offset is now forcibly suppressed (so no offset string is shown/offset_string stays empty) only if the set of distinct values taken by that field across the ticks includes the value 1 (e.g., a January tick when months vary); when those varying values do not include 1, the offset is kept displayed (show_offset stays on) even though the varying level is a year/month level.

On exit of the matplotlib.rc_context context manager, rcParams['backend'] is left untouched: whatever backend value (or resolution of the auto-backend sentinel) is in effect at the end of the context body is preserved after the context exits, rather than being restored to its value at context entry. In particular, an auto-backend sentinel present in the global rcParams at context entry is never re-installed into rcParams['backend'] by the context's cleanup, and a backend set or resolved inside the body (e.g. by figure creation, by the supplied fname/rc, or by matplotlib.use) is not rolled back.

When a Figure is pickled via __getstate__, the dpi value stored in the resulting pickled state under the '_dpi' key is the figure's original dpi (the '_original_dpi' recorded on its canvas when it was created) rather than the figure's current, possibly device-pixel-ratio-inflated dpi; consequently any inflation of the figure's dpi caused by HiDPI/Retina device-pixel-ratio scaling is discarded on pickling and not carried into the unpickled figure.

The align grouping in _get_aligned_offsets now pairs 'left' with 'bottom' (both on the offsets=[d,...] / descent-side branch) and 'right' with 'top' (both on the offsets=[height-h+d,...] branch), so that align='top' behaves like align='right' and align='bottom' behaves like align='left' within the shared helper.

When contourf()/QuadContourSet (filled=True) is drawn from a Z whose dtype is boolean and no contour levels are supplied, automatic level selection uses levels [0, 0.5, 1], so the resulting cs.levels equal [0, 0.5, 1].

For a DraggableBase instance d, d.canvas returns the canvas of d.ref_artist.figure (i.e. d.ref_artist.figure.canvas), resolved dynamically at access time rather than captured once at construction, so that .canvas still evaluates correctly (resolving to the re-attached figure's canvas) after the helper has been unpickled and re-attached to a figure; reads of self.canvas used for supports_blit checks, callback (dis)connection and canvas redraw/blit continue to work.
A Grouper instance whose _mapping holds weak references to live, weak-referenceable objects can be pickled (and unpickled, e.g. via pickle/copy.deepcopy) without raising an error.
When prepare_content_length is called with body=None on a request whose method is neither 'GET' nor 'HEAD' (e.g. POST), the 'Content-Length' header is still set to '0'.

prepend_scheme_if_needed preserves userinfo/authentication credentials embedded in the input URL across scheme prepending: when the URL's auth component (as parsed by urllib3's parse_url) is non-empty, the returned URL's authority (netloc, reconstructed via urlunparse) includes 'auth@' prefixed onto the host[:port] so the credentials are not dropped from the result.

PandasIndexAdapter exposes a new copy(deep=True) method that returns a new PandasIndexAdapter; with deep=True it wraps a deep copy of the underlying pandas index, with deep=False it shares the same underlying index, and in both cases the adapter's stored dtype is preserved on the returned adapter.

IndexVariable.to_index_variable() (and its to_coord alias) returns a new IndexVariable object that is distinct from the receiver rather than returning the receiver itself, so that mutating the returned variable (e.g. assigning its dims) does not change the dims of the IndexVariable it was called on.

When Dataset.set_index builds a new (multi-)index that supersedes an existing index, a coordinate variable belonging to the pre-existing (now-dropped) index — provided it is not among the variables being newly indexed and not itself recreated as one of the new index variables — is re-added to the resulting dataset as a regular de-indexed variable (via to_base_variable) instead of being removed from _variables, so no coordinate is silently deleted and referenced-coordinate integrity is preserved.

xr.where(cond, x, y, keep_attrs=True) where y is a Dataset and x is not a Dataset (x is promoted so the result is a Dataset): the result's top-level .attrs is set to {} (not to x.attrs), and the data variable of the result named by x.name, if x has a name present in the result's data_vars, is given x's attrs.

When PandasMultiIndexingAdapter.__array__ is called on an adapter whose level is set (not None), the returned numpy array is np.asarray(level_values.values, dtype=dtype) where dtype is the requested dtype argument if one was given, or otherwise the adapter's recorded dtype (self.dtype) — so the result has the requested dtype when one is supplied and otherwise preserves the recorded original level-coordinate dtype rather than whatever dtype pandas' get_level_values would otherwise produce (i.e., an int32 level coordinate is not upcast to int64).

In the dot (.dot) class diagram emitted by DotWriter.get_values / write_classes, each displayed method whose signature declares a type annotation on a positional argument other than `self` is rendered with that annotation as `methodname(argname: Type)`, pairing each annotation to its argument positionally; arguments without an annotation are rendered bare `argname` (multiple arguments joined by ', ').

pylint.exports a module-level Boolean constant `IS_PYPY` in `pylint.constants` that is True exactly when the running Python implementation is PyPy (as reported by `platform.python_implementation()`), and False otherwise.

When the PYLINTHOME environment variable is not set, the home directory resolves to a real path (USER_HOME is not "~"), and the legacy directory os.path.join(USER_HOME, ".pylint.d") already exists on disk, importing pylint.config prints a message to stderr stating that PYLINTHOME is now the new cache directory while the obsolescent old .pylint.d directory was found and can be safely removed (this is an existence check only — it does not create or delete the old directory).

Calling Similar.run() on an instance whose min_lines equals 0 returns immediately and does no similarity computation and produces no similarity report output on stdout (neither computed duplicates nor the TOTAL-lines summary line). Positive min_lines values still compute and display the report as before.

The help/usage text for the `--verbose` (`-v`) and `--enable-all-extensions` command-line options renders those flags with no argument value/metavar placeholder token following them (their per-option metavar is the empty string, threaded through the _CallableArgument conversion and add_argument call), instead of the default dest-derived uppercase placeholder.

expand_modules._is_ignored_file normalizes the given element path with os.path.normpath before deciding whether it is ignored, so an element whose literal text only matches an ignore-rule once redundant '.'/'..' segments, non-canonical separators, or trailing path separators are resolved is still treated as ignored: after the fix, an element path that does not literally match an ignore-paths regex (ignore_list_paths_re) but whose normalized form does is reported as ignored (previously it was not).

When get_unpacked_marks is called on a class with consider_mro=False, it returns only the marks declared directly on that class (its own pytestmark in its __dict__) and excludes any marks inherited from super-classes.

The function sklearn.decomposition.dict_learning() accepts a new keyword `method_max_iter` (default 1000) that is propagated as the `max_iter` of the sparse_encoding lasso solve performed in each dictionary-update step.

The single effective copy_X value resolved for a LassoLarsIC.fit call (explicit argument if given, else the estimator's copy_X attribute) is applied consistently to both the data preprocessing step (LinearModel._preprocess_data) and the lars_path call, so that whether the caller's input X array is copied or modified in place is governed by that one resolved value rather than being split between the two.

Under the refit=False (aggregation) path of LogisticRegressionCV.fit, when the penalty is not 'elasticnet', each class entry appended to self.l1_ratio_ is the value None (rather than being derived by indexing the internally-degenerate l1_ratios grid, which for non-elasticnet is the single-element [None] used as a dummy). Observable consequence: after fitting a non-elasticnet LogisticRegressionCV with refit=False, self.l1_ratio_ holds None values, matching the refit=True behavior.

When data_to_wrap is already a pandas DataFrame, _wrap_in_pandas_container ignores the index argument and preserves the input DataFrame's own existing index; it never reassigns data_to_wrap.index from the index parameter for DataFrame inputs. Consequently it does not raise a pandas 'Length mismatch' ValueError even when the supplied index is shorter/different in length from the DataFrame's rows. (Columns are still assigned in place when the columns argument is not None.)

roc_curve returns a `thresholds` array whose first element (the extra point added so the curve starts at fpr=0, tpr=0) is exactly `np.inf`, regardless of the values or magnitude of `y_score` (e.g. even when all scores are probabilities within [0,1], thresholds[0] is inf rather than max(y_score)+1, which was previously > 1 for fraction-scale scores).

Catalog.__iter__ yields Message objects whose locations list is sorted ascending by (source, line) — ordered lexicographically by source path and then by line number for a given source (previously the locations were in the insertion order of the underlying metadata entries).

When building the diagram's URL map in html_visit_inheritance_diagram from a resolved class reference (a pending_xref child carrying a 'refuri'): an external intersphinx reference (child with 'internal' falsy, i.e. not default/true) is recorded under the key equal to the substring of the refuri that follows its final '#', while an internal refuri-based reference is recorded under the key equal to its 'reftitle'.

A :glob: toctree pattern never adds a std-generated special page (genindex/modindex/search or any docname whose name coincides with a std label key) as a toctree entry/includefile, even when the glob pattern nominally matches that name.

In prepend_prolog, the set of leading content lines classified as the document's docinfo region (the lines after which the rst_prolog is inserted) is determined by matching each line against docutils' genuine field-list field-marker syntax (e.g. `:Field name: value`), rather than by the presence of any `:\w+:` token in the line. Concretely, while scanning from the top of `content`, a line advances `pos` (the prolog insertion index) only if that line is an actual field-marker entry; a heading or body line that merely contains an inline interpreted-text role form such as `:mod:\`title\`` inside its text is NOT treated as docinfo, so the prolog is inserted before it rather than after its role token.

The std domain's ':term:' cross-reference role no longer lowercases its reference text before use, so the term reference target stored on the pending_xref node (and matched against registered glossary terms) preserves the exact capitalization written in the reference instead of being case-folded.

When Sphinx parses a type annotation into cross-reference nodes (via sphinx.domains.python._parse_annotation, reached from both signature parameter annotations via _parse_arglist and return annotations via handle_signature), any bare-name text equal to the literal string 'None' is turned into a pending_xref node with refdomain='py', reftarget='None', and reftype='obj', so that 'None' is referenced as a Python object/data rather than as a class.
sphinx.pycode.ast.unparse() on an AST Tuple node whose elts list is empty returns the string '()' rather than the empty string that would result from joining zero element strings.

When rendering a C++ signature, a user-defined-literal's literal operator suffix identifier is shown as a (non-emphasised) plain text piece linked through a pending cross-reference whose reftarget is the literal-operator name `operator""IDENT`; correspondingly the description mode string 'udl' becomes acceptable to verify_description_mode so ASTIdentifier.describe_signature can be invoked in that mode.

DocstringSignatureMixin._find_signature recognizes an object's docstring signature when it is not located on the very first line of the object's docstring text: it scans the lines of each docstring block (skipping non-signature and empty lines) until it finds a signature whose base name matches the documented object, and treats the first such match as the signature.

Subscripting a _MockObject instance with a key of any type (not only str; e.g. an int, a type, or another non-string object) returns a new _MockObject subclass rather than raising an error, and the name of the resulting subclass is derived from str(key), i.e. the resulting subclass's __display_name__ equals the enclosing mock's __display_name__ + '.' + str(key).

When an automodule or autoclass directive is processed, the members explicitly named in a list-valued :private-members: or :special-members: option that are not already in the directive's :members: list are appended to it (so they are selected for member enumeration); this merging is skipped when :members: is given as a bare flag (ALL), and it happens both for ModuleDocumenter and ClassDocumenter.

In DocFieldTransformer.transform, when an otherwise-unknown/argument-mismatched typed field is still re-linked from its single-node text content, the resulting xref is now generated with the document's BuildEnvironment passed through, so that this fallback path applies the same domain field-xref processing and scope (py:module/py:class) as the standard doc-field xref path instead of producing an env-less xref.
Calls to sphinx.ext.autodoc.importer.get_module_members(module) now emit a RemovedInSphinx50Warning deprecation warning (while still returning the computed member list).

For Python object descriptions, the argument (variable name) of a :var:, :ivar:, or :cvar: doc field is rendered as plain literal bold text rather than as a cross-reference of role 'obj'; it no longer produces a pending cross-reference that would be resolved against module- and/or class-scoped Python objects bearing that name, and it is therefore never resolved to a same-named object of unrelated scope nor reported as a missing reference under nitpicky builds.

sphinx.ext.viewcode.collect_pages yields no viewcode pages (no per-module highlighted source pages and no '_modules/index' overview page) when the active builder is the singlehtml builder (builder.name == 'singlehtml').

For a class documented under an alias name (doc_as_attr), ClassDocumenter.get_doc returns an empty (non-None) docstring list when the class's real module source contains a module variable doc-comment for the alias name, and returns None when no such source comment exists. Consequently the alias is subjected to docstring processing (inherited autodoc-processing/autodoc-process-docstring applies to an empty docstring) only in the commented case, while an uncommented class alias still yields None and so performs no docstring processing.
For any non-empty input x, is_path_or_empty(x) validates x exactly as is_path does: it returns the (tilde-expanded) path if x resolves to an existing directory, and raises ValidationError otherwise.
The py:property directive accepts a ':classmethod:' flag option; providing it does not raise an unknown-option error.

The Literal-special handling applies only when the rendered base token of the bracketed subscript is exactly the bare name 'Literal' or the dotted 'typing.Literal'; for any other subscript base, value-argument text inside the brackets continues to be handled as ordinary type text (converted to type cross-reference nodes when non-whitespace, as before the patch).

Mock classes carry an explicit class-level __name__: a bare _MockObject instance exposes __name__ == '' (H0), while every subclass manufactured by _make_subclass (as returned by e.g. __getattr__/__getitem__ attribute access on a mock module or object, and used when a mocked class is used as a base) exposes __name__ equal to that member/attribute name (H2). Reading __name__ on a mock thus yields a real string value rather than falling back into __getattr__ and returning another mock.

Identity._entry(i, j) returns the KroneckerDelta(i, j) expression (left unevaluated) rather than a concrete scalar when Eq(i, j) evaluates to neither the boolean True object nor the boolean False object — i.e. when the indices are distinct symbolic/index expressions whose equality is not statically decidable (e.g. two independent symbols that could still be equal in value).

When an object that is already an instance of the requested class is passed to the constructor with an explicit size different from its own, the result is a new instance of that same class (subclass preserved) resized to the given size.

When Product._eval_product is applied to a term that is an Add whose as_numer_denom() yields a purely numeric (is_Number) denominator q — i.e. the term cannot be factored into independently-evaluable numerator/denominator products, such as n + 2**(-k) or n**(2/3) + 1 — the returned value is exp(Sum(log(p), (k, a, n))) / q (p being the numerator), rather than the sum over the separately-evaluated products of the numerator's individual Add addends.

In the generic Set._complement method, when the minuend argument (`other`) is a FiniteSet, elements of that FiniteSet for which the subtrahend (`self`) reports definitive containment (`self.contains(el)` evaluates to true) are removed from the result; elements the subtrahend reports as definitively-not-contained (`self.contains(el)` evaluates to false) are retained and constitute the ordinary FiniteSet members of the returned set.
