When mul_symbol is a custom string whose content is whitespace/empty once stripped, or is one of the LaTeX spacing commands r'\,', r'\:', r'\;', r'\quad', or a lone backslash r'\', the number-separator used when printing floats (mantissa-exponent form) and between adjacent numeric terms is the dot symbol (r' \cdot ') rather than the literal custom string.
polylog(0, z) auto-evaluates to z/(1 - z) for any z for which it is not already caught by the z=1, z=-1, or z=0 branches.

When tensor_product_simp is applied to a Mul whose sole non-commutative factor is a Pow whose base is a TensorProduct (possibly multiplied by commutative scalars), it returns the scalar multiplier times a TensorProduct in which the exponent is distributed into each argument, instead of returning the Mul unchanged.

When the first factor of a MatMul being LaTeX-printed is a negative number, output is a leading '-' followed by the space-joined rendering of the product obtained by using the absolute value of that coefficient with the remaining factors, so the negative coefficient is pulled out as a unary minus (e.g. MatMul(-1, A, B) renders as '-A B' rather than '-1 A B').

Printing an unevaluated Min expression (an object whose top-level func is Min, with more than one argument that Min does not collapse to a single symbol/numeral) via mathematica_code / MCodePrinter yields Mathematica function-call bracket notation of the form 'Min[arg1, arg2, ...]' rather than the parenthesized python-call form 'Min(arg1, arg2, ...)' that CodePrinter's fallback dispatch produces.

Add.is_zero (the _eval_is_zero handler) returns None rather than False for an Add belonging to a commutative (real-valued or complex-valued sum) whose classified arguments contain no real term known to be nonzero but contain at least one imaginary-direction term (an argument with is_imaginary, or whose product with the imaginary unit I is real), with any real arguments being individually known-zero; i.e. an expression whose real part is established as zero but whose full zero-ness (whether the imaginary part cancels) is not decidable is reported as unknown (None), not as nonzero (False).

For a symbol in MathMLPresentationPrinter._print_Symbol whose name decomposes into a base identifier plus subscript(s) and/or superscript(s) (e.g. Symbol('x2') -> base 'x', subscript '2'), the printed top-level element for that symbol is the structural element itself (an <msub> when only a subscript is present, an <msup> when only a superscript is present, or an <msubsup> when both are present), containing the base <mi> and the script content -- the structural element is no longer nested inside an outer <mi> wrapper.

When posify replaces a free symbol whose positivity is unknown with a positive dummy, the dummy carries over all of that symbol's other explicit assumptions (not only positive=True); consequently, querying the returned expression's replacement symbol for any of the original symbol's explicit assumptions (e.g., finite) yields the same truth value as on the original symbol, and likewise for other declared assumptions such as integer/rational/odd/even.

In the Add branch of _sqrt_match, the shortcut that delegates the expression to split_surds (returning split_surds' [a, b, r]) is taken only when the square of every addend is Rational AND positive; an Add whose addends' squares are all Rational but with at least one square non-positive (zero or negative) no longer takes that shortcut.

Left multiplication of a Point by a scalar factor (`factor * point`) yields a new Point whose coordinates are each the factor multiplied by the corresponding coordinate of `point`, sympified and simplified (i.e. behaves exactly the same as the corresponding right multiplication `point * factor`), rather than falling through to a generic SymPy Mul expression.

nthroot_mod(a, n, p) no longer raises NotImplementedError for composite (non-prime) modulus p with n != 2; instead it returns the sorted list of all distinct solutions x in [0, p) to x**n ≡ a (mod p), regardless of the all_roots flag.

The LaTeX rendering of a Subs expression always encloses the substituted expression (the LaTeX of subs.args[0], the expr being evaluated) in literal \left( ... \right) delimiters, so the emitted form is `\left. \left(<expr>\right) \right|_{\substack{ ... }}` regardless of what expr is.

Expression.__bool__ (truthiness of an EX ring element) returns falsy (False) whenever the wrapped SymPy expression f.ex is definitively zero, i.e. f.ex.is_zero is True, even when f.ex is not structurally equal to the Python integer 0; it returns truthy (True) in every other case (definitive nonzero or undecidable zero-ness).

Equality/identity evaluation between two generic Set instances (the multiple-dispatch _eval_is_eq rule matched when neither operand has a more-specific handler) is determined by mutual subsethood: it resolves to (the fuzzy logic of) whether lhs.is_subset(rhs) AND rhs.is_subset(lhs) are both true, in place of the previous blanket 'None' answer that left such equalities unevaluated.

split_super_sub still applies its trailing-digit exception when the given base name consists of one or more alphabetic characters immediately followed by a run of one or more digits: those trailing digits are removed from the returned name and prepended as the first element of the returned subs list. The alphabetic-prefix character condition is now Unicode-letter based ([^\W\d_], i.e. any non-digit, non-underscore word character), so the exception also fires for names whose letters include non-ASCII/Unicode characters (e.g. Greek), not just ASCII a-z/A-Z.

Mod.eval no longer propagates a PolynomialError raised by the internal gcd(p, q)/gcd_terms simplification step: when gcd(p, q) on the dividend/divisor arguments raises PolynomialError (e.g. piecewise-related generator issue), evaluation catches it, treats the extracted common factor G as 1 so that no gcd reduction is applied, and continues with the remainder of the Mod.eval simplification, ultimately returning a valid Mod result (an evaluated result or an unevaluated Mod form) instead of raising.

The zeros of the imaginary part im used to identify real members of an ImageSet are computed from the factors of numer(im) (the numerator when im is treated as a rational expression), so that real-valued members correspond to roots of that numerator; a purely rational/fractional form of im is reduced by its numerator rather than treated by its compounded-as-given factors.

In _print_Mul's unequal-fraction handling, a commutative denominator factor that is a Pow whose exponent is exactly -1 and whose base has more than one argument is parenthesized in the printed output when that base is itself a Pow (e.g. base = a**b), the same way bases that are a Mul already are. Concretely, an unevaluated product such as Mul(x, Pow(a**b, -1, evaluate=False)) prints its denominator 'a**b' wrapped in parentheses rather than unwrapped, so the affected term appears with surrounding parentheses in the rendered string.

AntiSymmetricTensor._latex renders as a brace-group enclosing the whole symbol with both its upper and lower indices, i.e. it returns '{%s^{%s}_{%s}}' formatting '{symbol^{upper}_{lower}}' rather than 'symbol^{upper}_{lower}'.

In CodePrinter._print_Mul, when an expression has a clearly-negative leading coefficient (sign '-') and its numerator reduces to exactly one factor, that lone factor is parenthesized against a weight strictly between PRECEDENCE['Mul'] and PRECEDENCE['Pow'] (0.5*(PRECEDENCE['Pow']+PRECEDENCE['Mul'])) rather than against the (Add-level) precedence of the negative Mul itself; consequently such a lone factor whose own precedence is below Pow-level (e.g. a Mul-level object) is now emitted inside parentheses directly after the leading '-'.

String is now a subclass of sympy.core.expr.Atom (in addition to Token), so every String instance (and its subclasses QuotedString and Comment) is an instance of Atom and exhibits SymPy atomic semantics (e.g. treated as an atom rather than a container by Basic traversal operations).

When PythonCodePrinter (and its subclass MpmathPrinter, both built atop AbstractPythonCodePrinter) prints a Min expression, the result is a call to the Python builtin min with the Min's arguments as comma-separated operands (i.e. code string of form `min(...)`), instead of the previous rewrite-to-Piecewise/`# Not supported` fallback.

The plain (non-mod-D) ZZ Hermite-normal-form computation steps through all rows of the matrix from bottom to top, not merely the bottom min(m, n) rows, and stops only once a pivot occupies every one of the n columns. Consequently, for an integer matrix with more rows than columns (m > n) whose genuinely nonzero row(s) lie above the bottom min(m, n) rows, the returned HNF keeps columns holding nonzero pivots obtained from those upper rows rather than returning a column-stripped (empty-column) result that discards them; e.g. hermite_normal_form of a ZZ matrix such as [[2,7],[0,0],[0,0]] returns a result retaining the top row's pivot column instead of an empty 3x0 result.
Contains(x, S).as_set() returns S (the set given as the second argument of the Contains) instead of raising NotImplementedError.
